sentences.zh: 列傳第五十七

translations.literal: Biographies, number fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: the 57th year of Biographies

sentences.zh: 胡穎徐度杜棱周鐵武程靈洗沈恪陸子隆錢道戢駱文牙孫瑒徐世譜周敷荀朗周炅魯悉達蕭摩訶任忠樊毅

translations.literal: Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, Zhou Tiewu, Cheng Lingxi, Shen Ke, Lu Zilong, Qian Daoji, Luo Wenya, Sun Yang, Xu Shipu, Zhou Fu, Xun Lang, Zhou Jiong, Lu Xida, Xiao Mohe, Ren Zhong, Fan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, Zhou Tiewu, Cheng Lingxi, Shen Ke, Lu Zilong, Qian Daoji, Luo Wenya, Sun Yang, Xu Shipu, Zhou Fu, Xun Lang, Zhou Jiong, Lu Xida, Xiao Mohe, Ren Zhong, and Fan Yi

sentences.zh: 梁承聖初，元帝授穎羅州刺史，封漢陽縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Liang era Chengsheng, Emperor Yuan appointed Ying Governor of Luozhou and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Hanyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang era Chengsheng, Emperor Yuan appointed Hu Ying governor of Luozhou and created him Marquis of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 尋除豫章內史，隨武帝鎮京口。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was removed and made Interior Minister of Yuzhang, following Emperor Wu in garrisoning Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made interior minister of Yuzhang and accompanied Chen Wudi when the latter took up his post at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 齊遣郭元建出東關，武帝令穎率府內驍勇隨侯瑱，于東關大破之。

translations.literal: Qi sent Guo Yuanjian out through Dongguan; Emperor Wu ordered Ying to lead the fierce warriors within the prefecture, following Hou Tian, and at Dongguan they routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi sent Guo Yuanjian through Dong Pass, Chen Wudi had Hu Ying lead the garrison’s best troops with Hou Tian and inflict a crushing defeat on the enemy at the pass.

sentences.zh: 後從武帝襲王僧辯，又隨周文育于吳興討杜龕。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wu in the surprise attack on Wang Sengbian, and again followed Zhou Wenyü in Wuxing to campaign against Du Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Chen Wudi in the coup against Wang Sengbian and followed Zhou Wenyü to Wuxing in the campaign against Du Kan.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，兼左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, [Ying] concurrently served as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi took the throne, Hu Ying was also appointed general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，除散騎常侍，吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, he was removed [from office] and made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng (560), he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was given the posthumous name Zhuang (“Stalwart”).

sentences.zh: 二年，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was granted paired sacrifice in Emperor Wu’s temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was given a place in the sacrifices at Chen Wudi’s temple.

sentences.zh: 子六同嗣。

translations.literal: His son Liutong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liutong inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 徐度字孝節，安陸人也。

translations.literal: Xu Du, style name Xiaojie, was a native of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Du, courtesy name Xiaojie, was from Anlu.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，不拘小節。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and unrestrained, not bound by petty proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and free-spirited, caring little for petty conventions.

sentences.zh: 及長，姿貌瑰偉，嗜酒好博，恒使僮僕屠酤為事。

translations.literal: When grown, his bearing was magnificent and imposing; he loved wine and gambling, and constantly had his servants butcher and sell wine as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he was striking in appearance, fond of wine and gambling, and regularly had his servants run a butcher shop and tavern.

sentences.zh: 初從梁始興內史蕭介征諸山洞，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: At first he followed Liang’s Interior Minister of Shixing, Xiao Jie, in campaigns against the various mountain caves, and became known for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Xiao Jie, interior minister of Shixing under the Liang, in campaigns against the hill tribes and won a reputation for martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝征交址，乃委質焉。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi campaigned against Jiaozhi, he then offered his allegiance there.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi campaigned in Jiaozhi, Xu Du submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，武帝克廣州，平蔡路養，破李遷仕，計畫多出於度。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing’s rebellion, Emperor Wu captured Guangzhou, pacified Cai Luyang, and defeated Li Qianshi; plans for these came largely from Du.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing’s rebellion, Chen Wudi’s capture of Guangzhou and victories over Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi owed much to Xu Du’s planning.

sentences.zh: 侯景平後，追錄前後戰功，封廣德縣侯。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, his earlier and later battle merits were recorded retrospectively, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde County.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing’s defeat, his past and recent military achievements were recognized and he was created Marquis of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 武帝鎮朱方，除蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu garrisoned Zhufang, [Du] was removed [from office] and made Governor of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi held Zhufang, Xu Du was appointed governor of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣衡陽獻王往荊州，度率所領從焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sent the Prince of Hengyang Xian to Jingzhou; Du led the troops under his command and followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi sent the Prince of Hengyang to Jingzhou, Xu Du led his command and went with him.

sentences.zh: 江陵覆亡，間行東歸。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he made his way east by secret routes.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Jiangling he made his way back east by hidden routes.

sentences.zh: 武帝東討杜龕，奉敬帝幸京口，以度領宿衛，並知留府事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu campaigned east against Du Kan, escorting Emperor Jing to Jingkou; Du was put in charge of the night guard and also directed affairs left at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi marched east against Du Kan and escorted Emperor Jing to Jingkou, Xu Du commanded the palace guard and managed affairs at the capital in the emperor’s absence.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約等來寇，武帝與敬帝還都，時賊已據石頭，使度頓軍於冶城寺。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui, Ren Yue, and others came raiding; Emperor Wu and Emperor Jing returned to the capital; at the time the rebels already held Shitou, and [Wu] had Du encamp his army at Yecheng Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Sihui and Ren Yue attacked, Chen Wudi and Emperor Jing returned to the capital; the rebels already held Stone City, and Xu Du was ordered to encamp at Yecheng Temple.

sentences.zh: 明年，嗣徽等又引齊寇濟江，度隨眾軍破之於北郊壇。

translations.literal: The next year, Sihui and the others again brought Qi raiders across the river; Du followed the massed armies and defeated them at the North Suburban Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Sihui again brought Qi forces across the Yangzi; Xu Du joined the main army in defeating them at the North Suburban Altar.

sentences.zh: 以功除郢州刺史，兼領吳興太守。

translations.literal: For his merit he was removed [from office] and made Governor of Yingzhou, concurrently holding the post of Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was made governor of Yingzhou and also held Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，累遷侍中、中撫將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, [Du] was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Center, and Grand Master with golden tally equal to the Three Excellencies with an open office, and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen he rose to palace attendant, general who pacifies the center, and grand master with golden tally equal to the three excellencies with an open office, and was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，以平王琳功，改封湘東郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, for merit in pacifying Wang Lin, his fief was changed to Duke of Xiangdong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng (560), for his role in defeating Wang Lin, he was created Duke of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 及太尉侯瑱薨於湘州，以度代瑱為都督、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: When Grand Marshal Hou Tian died in Xiangzhou, Du was made to replace Tian as Area Commander and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Hou Tian died in Xiangzhou, Xu Du succeeded him as area commander and governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，復為侍中、中軍大將軍。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he again became Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to court as palace attendant and grand general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 文帝崩，度預顧命，許以甲仗五十人入殿省。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, Du was included in the deathbed testament; he was permitted fifty armed men with armor to enter the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Wen’s deathbed Xu Du was named to the regency council and allowed fifty armed guards in the palace.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，進位司空。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, [Du] was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Fei acceded, Xu Du was promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太尉，諡曰忠肅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Grand Marshal; his posthumous title was Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand marshal with the posthumous name Zhongsu (“Loyal and Solemn”).

sentences.zh: 太建四年，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian, he was granted paired sacrifice in Emperor Wu’s temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taijian (572) he was given a place in the sacrifices at Chen Wudi’s temple.

sentences.zh: 子敬成嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jingcheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingcheng inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 敬成幼聰慧，好讀書。

translations.literal: Jingcheng in youth was clever and intelligent, fond of reading books.
translations.idiomatic: Jingcheng was clever as a child and loved to read.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as assistant gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永定元年，領度所部士卒，隨周文育、侯安都征王琳，於沌口敗績，為琳所縶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongding, he led the troops under Du’s command, following Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu in campaigning against Wang Lin; at Dundu they suffered defeat and were seized by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongding (557) he led his father’s troops with Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu against Wang Lin, was defeated at Dundu, and taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 二年，隨文育、安都得歸。

translations.literal: In the second year, he followed Wenyü and Andu in returning.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned with Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu.

sentences.zh: 父度為吳郡太守，以敬成監郡。

translations.literal: His father Du was Governor of Wu Commandery; Jingcheng was made to supervise the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When his father became governor of Wu, Jingcheng was appointed to supervise the commandery in his stead.

sentences.zh: 光大元年，為巴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangda, he became Governor of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangda (567) he was made governor of Ba.

sentences.zh: 尋為水軍，隨吳明徹平華皎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served in the navy, following Wu Mingche in pacifying Hua Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the navy under Wu Mingche in the campaign against Hua Jiao.

sentences.zh: 二年，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: In the second year, on account of his father’s mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 尋起為南豫州刺史，襲爵湘東郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to serve as Governor of South Yuzhou and inherited the title Duke of Xiangdong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as governor of South Yu and inherited the dukedom of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，除吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, he was removed [from office] and made Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian (573) he was made governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 隨都督吳明徹北討，出秦郡，別遣敬成為都督，乘金翅自歐陽引埭泝江，由廣陵，齊人皆城守，弗敢出。

translations.literal: He followed Area Commander Wu Mingche on the northern campaign; exiting Qin Commandery, [Mingche] separately dispatched Jingcheng as commander, boarding the Golden Wings from Ouyangyin Dam upstream along the river, via Guangling; the Qi people all held their cities and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Wu Mingche’s northern campaign; detached as a separate commander, he sailed the Golden Wings upstream from Ouyangyin Dam through Guangling while the Qi garrisons held their walls and dared not sally forth.

sentences.zh: 自繁梁湖下淮，克淮陰、山陽、鹽城三郡，仍進克鬱洲。

translations.literal: From Fanliang Lake he descended the Huai, captured the three commanderies of Huaiyin, Shanyang, and Yancheng, and then advanced to capture Yuzhou as well.
translations.idiomatic: From Fanliang Lake he descended the Huai, took Huaiyin, Shanyang, and Yancheng, and then captured Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 進號壯武將軍，鎮朐山。

translations.literal: He was advanced in title to General of Stalwart Martiality and garrisoned Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of stalwart martiality and stationed at Qushan.

sentences.zh: 坐於軍中輒科訂，並誅新附者，免官。

translations.literal: He was punished for on his own authority imposing fines and punishments in the army and executing those newly submitted; he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for arbitrarily imposing fines in camp and executing newly submitted troops.

sentences.zh: 尋除安州刺史，鎮宿預。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed [from office] and made Governor of Anzhou, garrisoning Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of An and stationed at Suyu.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰思。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Si.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Si (“Reflective”).

sentences.zh: 子敞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 杜棱字雄盛，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Du Leng, style name Xiongsheng, was a native of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Leng, courtesy name Xiongsheng, was from Qiantang in Wu.

sentences.zh: 少落泊，不為時知。

translations.literal: In youth he was down and out, unknown to his age.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was obscure and went unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 頗涉書傳。

translations.literal: He had considerable exposure to books and chronicles.
translations.idiomatic: He had read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 游嶺南，事梁廣州刺史新渝侯蕭映。

translations.literal: He traveled to Lingnan and served Liang’s Governor of Guangzhou, the Marquis of Xinyü, Xiao Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He went south to Lingnan and entered the service of Xiao Ying, Marquis of Xinyü and governor of Guangzhou under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 映卒，從陳武帝，平蔡路養、李遷仕皆有功。

translations.literal: When Ying died, [Leng] followed Chen Wudi; in pacifying Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi he had merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Ying’s death he followed Chen Wudi and distinguished himself in the campaigns against Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制，授石州刺史、上陌縣侯。

translations.literal: When Liang’s Emperor Yuan assumed the regency, he appointed [Leng] Governor of Shizhou and Marquis of Shangmo County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him governor of Shi and Marquis of Shangmo.

sentences.zh: 侯景平後，武帝鎮朱方，以棱監義興、琅邪二郡。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Wu garrisoned Zhufang and made Leng overseer of the two commanderies of Yixing and Langye.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing’s defeat, when Chen Wudi held Zhufang, Du Leng was put in charge of Yixing and Langye.

sentences.zh: 武帝謀誅王僧辯，引棱與侯安都等共議，棱難之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu plotted to execute Wang Sengbian and drew in Leng with Hou Andu and others to deliberate together; Leng found it difficult [to agree].
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi plotted to kill Wang Sengbian, he consulted Du Leng and Hou Andu among others; Du Leng objected.

sentences.zh: 武帝懼其泄己，乃以手巾絞棱，棱悶絕於地，因閉於別室。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu feared he would leak [the plot] and so strangled Leng with a hand towel; Leng lost consciousness on the ground and was then shut in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Du Leng would betray the plot, Chen Wudi throttled him with a towel until he collapsed, then locked him in a side room.

sentences.zh: 軍發，召與同行。

translations.literal: When the army set out, [Wu] summoned him to travel together.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched, he was brought along under guard.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯平後，武帝東征杜龕等，留棱與安都居守。

translations.literal: After Sengbian was pacified, Emperor Wu campaigned east against Du Kan and the others, leaving Leng and Andu to hold and guard [the capital].
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Sengbian’s death Chen Wudi marched east against Du Kan, leaving Du Leng and Hou Andu to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約引齊師濟江，攻台城，安都與棱隨方抗拒，未嘗解帶。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue brought Qi troops across the river, attacking the capital city; Andu and Leng resisted as circumstances required, never undoing their belts [to rest].
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Sihui and Ren Yue brought Qi forces across the Yangzi to attack the capital, Hou Andu and Du Leng held the defenses day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功除右衛將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, for his merit he was removed [from office] and made General of the Right Guard and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated he was made general of the right guard and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 棱曆事三帝，並見恩寵。

translations.literal: Leng served three emperors in succession and in all received favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: Du Leng served three emperors and enjoyed favor at each court.

sentences.zh: 末年不預征役，優遊都下。

translations.literal: In his later years he did not take part in campaigns; he lived at ease in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years he was excused from campaigns and lived at ease in the capital.

sentences.zh: 頃之，卒於官。

translations.literal: Before long, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，諡曰成，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Master with golden tally equal to the Three Excellencies with an open office; his posthumous title was Cheng; he was granted paired sacrifice in Emperor Wu’s temple court.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand master with golden tally equal to the three excellencies with an open office, given the posthumous name Cheng (“Accomplished”), and granted a place in the sacrifices at Chen Wudi’s temple.

sentences.zh: 子安世嗣。

translations.literal: His son Anshi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anshi inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 周鐵武，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Tiewu—of what place he was is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tiewu was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 語音傖重，膂力過人，便馬槊。

translations.literal: His speech was thick and northern; his physical strength surpassed other men; he was skilled with horse and spear.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with a heavy northern accent, possessed extraordinary strength, and was expert with horse and lance.

sentences.zh: 事梁河東王蕭譽，以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: He served Liang’s Prince of Hedong, Xiao Yu, and became known for courage.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xiao Yu, Prince of Hedong under the Liang, and won fame for bravery.

sentences.zh: 譽為湘州，以為臨蒸令。

translations.literal: When Yu held Xiangzhou, [Yu] made him Magistrate of Linzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yu governed Xiangzhou he appointed Zhou Tiewu magistrate of Linzheng.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，梁元帝遣世子方等伐譽，譽拒戰，大捷，方等死，鐵武功最。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing’s rebellion, Liang’s Emperor Yuan sent the heir Fangdeng to campaign against Yu; Yu resisted in battle and won a great victory; Fangdeng died, and Tiewu’s merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing’s rebellion Emperor Yuan of Liang sent his heir Fangdeng against Xiao Yu; Yu routed the imperial army and killed Fangdeng, and Zhou Tiewu’s exploits were foremost.

sentences.zh: 及王僧辯討譽，於陣獲之，將烹焉，鐵武呼曰：「侯景未滅，奈何殺壯士！」

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Yu, [Sengbian] captured him in battle and was about to boil him alive; Tiewu cried out: “Hou Jing is not yet destroyed—how can you kill a stalwart warrior!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian attacked Xiao Yu, Zhou Tiewu was captured and about to be executed; he cried out, "Hou Jing is not yet destroyed—why kill a brave man!

sentences.zh: 僧辯奇其言，宥之，還其麾下。

translations.literal: Sengbian marveled at his words, pardoned him, and returned him to his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian was impressed, spared him, and restored him to his command.

sentences.zh: 及侯景西上，鐵武從僧辯克任約，獲宋子仙，每戰有功。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing marched west, Tiewu followed Sengbian in defeating Ren Yue, capturing Song Zixian; in every battle he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing marched west, Zhou Tiewu followed Wang Sengbian in defeating Ren Yue and capturing Song Zixian, distinguishing himself in every battle.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，授潼州刺史，封沌陽縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan assumed the regency, he appointed [Tiewu] Governor of Tongzhou and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Dunyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan appointed him governor of Tong and created him Viscount of Dunyang.

sentences.zh: 又從僧辯定建鄴，降謝答仁，平陸納於湘州，錄前後功，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Again he followed Sengbian in securing Jianye, accepting the surrender of Xie Daren, and pacifying Lu Na in Xiangzhou; his earlier and later merits were recorded, and his rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Sengbian in taking Jiankang, accepting Xie Daren’s surrender and defeating Lu Na in Xiangzhou, and was advanced to marquis for his cumulative service.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝誅僧辯，鐵武率所部降，因復其本職。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi executed Sengbian, Tiewu led the troops under his command in surrender and thereby had his original post restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi killed Wang Sengbian, Zhou Tiewu surrendered with his troops and was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽引齊寇度江，鐵武破其水軍。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui brought Qi raiders across the river; Tiewu defeated their navy.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Sihui brought Qi forces across the Yangzi, Zhou Tiewu routed their fleet.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽平，遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: When Sihui was pacified, [Tiewu] was transferred to Colonel of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Sihui’s defeat he was made colonel of the left guard of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋隨周文育拒蕭勃，文育命鐵武偏軍襲勃，禽勃前軍歐陽頠。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Zhou Wenyü in resisting Xiao Bo; Wenyü ordered Tiewu with a detached force to strike Bo and captured Bo’s vanguard Ouyang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Zhou Wenyü against Xiao Bo; sent with a detached force, he captured Bo’s vanguard Ouyang Yi.

sentences.zh: 又隨文育西征王琳於沌口，敗績，與文育、侯安都並為琳所禽。

translations.literal: Again he followed Wenyü west in campaigning against Wang Lin at Dundu; they suffered defeat, and together with Wenyü and Hou Andu he was captured by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Zhou Wenyü’s western campaign against Wang Lin at Dundu, was defeated, and was captured along with Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu.

sentences.zh: 琳見諸將與語，唯鐵武辭氣不屈，故琳盡宥文育之徒，獨鐵武見害。

translations.literal: Lin saw the generals and spoke with them; only Tiewu’s words and bearing were unyielding; therefore Lin pardoned Wenyü’s party entirely but Tiewu alone was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin spoke with the captured generals; only Zhou Tiewu answered defiantly, so Lin spared the others but executed Zhou Tiewu alone.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、護軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant and Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 天嘉五年，文帝又詔配食武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiancheng, Emperor Wen again ordered him granted food-offering sacrifice in Emperor Wu’s temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiancheng (564) Emperor Wen again granted him a place in the sacrifices at Chen Wudi’s temple.

sentences.zh: 子瑜嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 程靈洗字玄滌，新安海寧人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Lingxi, style name Xuandi, was a native of Haining in Xin’an.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lingxi, courtesy name Xuandi, was from Haining in Xin’an.

sentences.zh: 少以勇力聞，步行日二百里，便騎善遊，素為鄉里畏伏。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for courage and strength; on foot he could cover two hundred li in a day; he was skilled at riding and swimming; from of old the village feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Known from youth for strength and daring, he could walk two hundred li in a day, was expert rider and swimmer, and was feared throughout his district.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，據黟、歙聚徒以拒景。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing’s rebellion, he held Yi and She, gathering followers to resist Jing.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing’s rebellion he held Yi and She and raised a force to resist him.

sentences.zh: 景軍據有新安，新安太守湘西鄉侯蕭隱奔依靈洗，靈洗奉以主盟。

translations.literal: Jing’s army held Xin’an; the Governor of Xin’an, the Marquis of Xiangxi Township, Xiao Yin, fled to rely on Lingxi; Lingxi received him as alliance leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing’s troops took Xin’an, the governor Xiao Yin, Marquis of Xiangxi, fled to Cheng Lingxi, who accepted him as leader of the resistance.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝授靈洗譙州刺史資，領新安太守，封巴丘縣侯。

translations.literal: Liang’s Emperor Yuan appointed Lingxi with the salary of Governor of Qiaozhou, concurrently holding the post of Governor of Xin’an, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Baqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him governor of Qiao with the salary of that office, made him acting governor of Xin’an, and created him Marquis of Baqiu.

sentences.zh: 後助王僧辯鎮防。

translations.literal: Later he assisted Wang Sengbian in garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: He later assisted Wang Sengbian in garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 及武帝誅僧辯，靈洗率所領來援，其夜力戰於石頭西門，武帝軍不利，遣使招喻，久之乃降，帝深義之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu executed Sengbian, Lingxi led the troops under his command to come to the rescue; that night they fought fiercely at the west gate of Shitou; Emperor Wu’s army was unfavorable; he sent envoys to summon and persuade; only after long [negotiation] did [Lingxi] surrender; the Emperor deeply honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi killed Wang Sengbian, Cheng Lingxi marched to his relief and fought fiercely at the west gate of Stone City that night; when Chen’s forces faltered, envoys were sent to negotiate, and after prolonged talks Cheng Lingxi surrendered, which Chen Wudi deeply respected.

sentences.zh: 授蘭陵太守，仍助防京口。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Lanling and still assisted in defending Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Lanling and continued to help defend Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 及平徐嗣徽，靈洗有功，除南丹陽太守，封遂安縣侯。

translations.literal: When Xu Sihui was pacified, Lingxi had merit; he was removed [from office] and made Governor of South Danyang and enfeoffed as Marquis of Suian County.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in defeating Xu Sihui he was made governor of South Danyang and Marquis of Suian.

sentences.zh: 後隨周文育西討王琳，軍敗，為琳所拘。

translations.literal: Later he followed Zhou Wenyü west in campaigning against Wang Lin; the army was defeated and he was detained by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Zhou Wenyü’s campaign against Wang Lin in the west, was defeated, and taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 尋與侯安都等逃歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he escaped and returned together with Hou Andu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon escaped and returned with Hou Andu and the others.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Colonel of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel of the left guard of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 武帝崩，王琳前軍東下，靈洗于南陵破之，虜其兵士，並獲青龍十餘乘。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu died. Wang Lin's vanguard advanced east. Ling Xi defeated them at Nanling, captured their soldiers, and also seized more than ten Green Dragon [chariots].
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Wudi's death, Wang Lin's vanguard marched east. Cheng Lingxi routed them at Nanling, took their soldiers prisoner, and captured more than a dozen Green Dragon war chariots as well.

sentences.zh: 以功授都督、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Area Commander and Governor of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was made area commander and governor of South Yu.

sentences.zh: 侯瑱等敗王琳於柵口，靈洗逐北，據有魯山。

translations.literal: Hou Tian and others defeated Wang Lin at Shankou. Ling Xi pursued the fleeing enemy and seized Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Tian and his colleagues defeated Wang Lin at Shankou, Cheng Lingxi pursued the broken army and took Lushan.

sentences.zh: 徵為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 天嘉四年，周迪重寇臨川，以靈洗為都督，自鄱陽別道擊之，迪又走山谷間。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng, Zhou Di again raided Linchuan. Ling Xi was made Area Commander and attacked him by a separate route from Poyang. Zhou Di fled again into the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiancheng (563), Zhou Di again invaded Linchuan. Cheng Lingxi was appointed area commander and struck at him by a detour from Poyang, driving Zhou Di back into the hills.

sentences.zh: 遷中護軍，出為都督、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Central Protector of the Army and went out to serve as Area Commander and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to central protector of the army, then sent out as area commander and governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，進號雲麾將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Fei acceded, his title was advanced to General of the Clouded Banners.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Fei came to the throne, Cheng Lingxi's rank was raised to general of the clouded banners.

sentences.zh: 華皎之反，遣使招靈洗，靈洗斬皎使以聞。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao rebelled, he sent envoys to recruit Ling Xi. Ling Xi executed Jiao's envoys and reported this to the court.
translations.idiomatic: During Hua Jiao's rebellion, Jiao sent messengers to win Cheng Lingxi over. Cheng Lingxi beheaded the envoys and reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朝廷深嘉其忠，因推心待之，使其子文季領水軍助防。

translations.literal: The court deeply praised his loyalty and hence treated him with complete trust, having his son Wenji lead the river forces to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The court greatly admired his loyalty and treated him with unreserved trust, assigning his son Wenji to command the river fleet in the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 時周將元定率步騎二萬助皎，圍靈洗，靈洗嬰城固守。

translations.literal: At the time the Zhou general Yuan Ding led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to aid Jiao and besieged Ling Xi. Ling Xi closed the city gates and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou general Yuan Ding then arrived with twenty thousand foot and horse to support Jiao and laid siege to Cheng Lingxi, who shut the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 及皎敗，乃出軍躡定，定不獲濟江，以其眾降。

translations.literal: When Jiao was defeated, he then led his army in pursuit of Ding. Ding could not cross the Yangzi and surrendered with his troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao's defeat, Cheng Lingxi sallied forth in pursuit of Yuan Ding. Unable to cross the Yangzi, Ding surrendered with his entire force.

sentences.zh: 因進攻，克周沔州，禽其刺史裴寬。

translations.literal: He then pressed the attack, captured Zhou's Mianzhou, and took its governor Pei Kuan prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on, he captured Mian Prefecture from Zhou and took its governor, Pei Kuan, alive.

sentences.zh: 以功改封重安縣公。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: For these services his fief was changed to Duke of Chong'an.

sentences.zh: 靈洗性嚴急，禦下甚苛刻，士卒有小罪，必以軍法誅之。

translations.literal: Ling Xi was stern and harsh by nature; he was very severe toward subordinates, and soldiers guilty of even minor offenses were invariably executed by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lingxi was severe and impatient by nature. Toward those under his command he was unsparing: the smallest breach of discipline was punished by death under military law.

sentences.zh: 號令分明，與士卒同甘苦，眾亦以此德之。

translations.literal: His orders were clear and distinct, and he shared hardship and comfort with his soldiers; the men also respected him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his commands were clear, and he shared every hardship with his troops; for this the men held him in genuine esteem.

sentences.zh: 性好播植，躬勤耕稼，至於水陸所宜，刈獲早晚，雖老農不能及也。

translations.literal: He loved planting and cultivating; he personally worked hard at farming. As for what suited dry or wet land, the timing of harvests—even old farmers could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved sowing and planting and worked the fields himself. In knowing what to grow on wet or dry ground, and when to reap, he surpassed even the oldest farmers.

sentences.zh: 妓妾無遊手，並督之紡績。

translations.literal: No concubine or attendant was idle; he all set them to spinning and weaving under supervision.
translations.idiomatic: None of his concubines or attendants was permitted to idle; he set them all to spinning and weaving under his eye.

sentences.zh: 至於散用貲財，亦弗儉吝。

translations.literal: When it came to distributing wealth and goods, he was not stingy either.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to dispensing money and goods, he was no less generous.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮西將軍、開府儀同三司，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master with golden tally equal to the Three Excellencies; his posthumous title was Loyal and Stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made general who pacifies the west and grand master with golden tally equal to the three excellencies, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang ("Loyal and Stalwart").

sentences.zh: 太建四年，配享武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian, he was granted paired sacrifice in Emperor Wu's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taijian (572) he was given a place in the sacrifices at Chen Wudi's temple.

sentences.zh: 子文季嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wenji succeeded to his title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenji inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 文季字少卿，幼習騎射，多幹略，果決有父風。

translations.literal: Wenji, courtesy name Shaoqing, had studied riding and archery from childhood; he possessed much practical talent and was resolute and decisive, showing his father's character.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji, courtesy name Shaoqing, had trained in horsemanship and archery from boyhood. He was resourceful and resolute, bearing his father's stamp.

sentences.zh: 靈洗與周文育、侯安都等敗於沌口，為王琳所執，武帝召陷賊諸將子弟厚遇之，文季最有禮容，深見賞。

translations.literal: When Ling Xi, together with Zhou Wenyü, Hou Andu and others, was defeated at Dundu and captured by Wang Lin, Emperor Wu summoned the sons of the generals who had fallen into enemy hands and treated them generously. Wenji had the finest bearing and manners and was deeply appreciated.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Lingxi, Zhou Wenyü, Hou Andu, and the rest were defeated at Dundu and taken by Wang Lin, Chen Wudi summoned the sons of the captured generals and treated them with special kindness. Wenji, the most courteous and composed among them, won his particular favor.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，除宣惠始興王府限內中直兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Wenji was appointed military attendant of the interior direct guard within the confines of the Princely Establishment of Xuanhui, Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Wenji was appointed military attendant of the interior guard within the household of Xuanhui, Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 累遷臨海太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to governor of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 後乘金翅助父鎮郢城。

translations.literal: Later he sailed the Golden Wings to assist his father in guarding Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sailed the warship Golden Wings to help his father hold Ying.

sentences.zh: 華皎平，靈洗及文季並有扞禦之功。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao was suppressed, both Ling Xi and Wenji had merits in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao was put down, both Cheng Lingxi and Wenji were credited with distinguished service in the defense.

sentences.zh: 及靈洗卒，文季盡領其眾。

translations.literal: When Ling Xi died, Wenji took full command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheng Lingxi's death, Wenji assumed full command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 起為超武將軍，仍助防郢州。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Superlative Martial Prowess and continued to assist in the defense of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to general of superlative martial prowess and continued to assist in the defense of Ying.

sentences.zh: 文季性至孝，雖軍旅奪禮，而毀瘠甚至。

translations.literal: Wenji was extremely filial by nature. Though military service had disrupted the mourning rites, he became emaciated from grief to an extreme degree.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji was profoundly filial. Though camp and campaign had torn him from the rites of mourning, he wasted away in grief to an alarming degree.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲封重安縣公。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Chong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was complete, he succeeded to the dukedom of Chong'an.

sentences.zh: 隨都督章昭達率軍往荊州征梁。

translations.literal: He followed Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda, leading troops to Jingzhou to campaign against Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed area commander Zhang Zhaoda at the head of an army into Jingzhou to campaign against Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁人與周軍多造舟艦，置於青泥水中，昭達遣文季共錢道戢盡焚其舟艦。

translations.literal: The Liang people and Zhou forces had built many boats and ships, mooring them in the waters of Qingni. Zhang Zhaoda sent Wenji together with Qian Daoji to burn all their boats and ships.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang and Zhou armies had built a great fleet and anchored it in the Qingni waters. Zhang Zhaoda dispatched Wenji, together with Qian Daoji, to burn every vessel.

sentences.zh: 既而周兵大出，文季僅以身免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Zhou armies came out in force; Wenji barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou armies then poured out in strength, and Wenji barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 以功加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Directness.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was further made regular attendant of unimpeded directness.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，都督吳明徹北討，至秦郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, Area Commander Wu Mingche launched a northern expedition and reached Qin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian (573), area commander Wu Mingche marched north on campaign and reached Qin Commandery.

sentences.zh: 秦郡前江浦通塗水，齊人並下大柱為杙，柵水中。

translations.literal: Before Qin Commandery, the Jiangpu connected with Tushui. The Qi people had driven great pillars as piles and built a barrier in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Before Qin Commandery the Jiangpu joined the Tushui, where the Qi had sunk great pillars as stakes and barred the channel.

sentences.zh: 文季乃前領驍勇，拔開其柵，明徹率大軍自後而至，攻克秦郡。

translations.literal: Wenji then advanced at the head of elite troops, tore open the barrier, and Mingche led the main army up from behind and captured Qin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji led the elite vanguard forward, broke through the barrier, and Wu Mingche brought up the main force from behind to take Qin Commandery.

sentences.zh: 又別遣文季攻涇州，屠其城。

translations.literal: He also separately dispatched Wenji to attack Jing Prefecture and slaughtered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Wenji separately against Jing Prefecture, which was taken and put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 進拔盱眙。

translations.literal: He then advanced and captured Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on and captured Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 仍隨明徹圍壽陽。

translations.literal: He continued to follow Mingche in besieging Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Wu Mingche in the siege of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 文季臨事謹飭，禦下嚴整，前後所克城壘，率皆迮水為堰，土木之功，動踰數萬。

translations.literal: Wenji was careful and disciplined in affairs, stern and orderly toward subordinates. Of the fortifications he captured before and after, nearly all had dams built of compressed earth and water; the labor in earthworks and timber regularly exceeded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji was meticulous in action and strict with his men. In every fortress he took, he habitually built earth-and-water dams; the earthworks and timber required routinely ran to tens of thousands of man-days.

sentences.zh: 置陣役人，文季必先于諸將，夜則早起，迄暮不休，軍中莫不服其勤幹。

translations.literal: When labor was assigned for battle formations, Wenji always went ahead of the other generals; he rose early in the morning and worked without rest until evening. No one in the army failed to admire his diligence and competence.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever troops were levied for entrenchment and siege work, Wenji always outpaced the other commanders—up before dawn and laboring without pause until nightfall. The whole army marveled at his industry.

sentences.zh: 每戰為前鋒，齊軍深憚之，謂為程彪。

translations.literal: In every battle he served as the vanguard. The Qi army greatly feared him and called him "Cheng Biao."
translations.idiomatic: In every fight he led the van. The Qi feared him deeply and nicknamed him "Cheng the Tiger."

sentences.zh: 以功除散騎常侍，帶新安內史。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Interior Minister of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrently interior minister of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 累遷北徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Governor of North Xuzhou, with the additional title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to governor of North Xu and given the additional title of area commander.

sentences.zh: 後隨明徹北侵，軍敗，為周所囚，仍授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he followed Mingche on a northern invasion, the army was defeated, he was taken prisoner by Zhou, and was nevertheless granted Grand Master with golden tally equal to the Three Excellencies with an open office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on Wu Mingche's northern campaign, the army was broken and Wenji was taken by Zhou—yet Zhou still invested him as grand master with golden tally equal to the three excellencies with an open office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，自周逃歸，至渦陽，為邊吏執送長安，死於獄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he fled back from Zhou, reached Woyang, was seized by border officials and sent to Chang'an, and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he escaped from Zhou and fled as far as Woyang, where border officials seized him and sent him to Chang'an. He died in prison.

sentences.zh: 是時既與周絕，不之知。

translations.literal: At that time Chen had already broken off relations with Zhou, so they did not know of this.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chen had already severed ties with Zhou, and the court knew nothing of his fate.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，後主知之，贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide, when the Later Lord learned of it, he posthumously granted him Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide (583), when Emperor Houzhu learned what had happened, he posthumously made Wenji regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又詔傷其廢絕，降封重安縣侯，以子響襲封。

translations.literal: An edict also lamented that his line had been cut off and reduced the enfeoffment to Marquis of Chong'an County, with his son Xiang inheriting the title.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also mourned the extinction of his line, reduced the fief to Marquis of Chong'an, and had his son Xiang inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 沈恪字子恭，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Ke, courtesy name Zigong, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ke, courtesy name Zigong, was from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 深沈有幹局。

translations.literal: He was deep and reserved, with administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was deep-minded and steady, with a talent for practical administration.

sentences.zh: 梁新渝侯蕭映之為廣州，兼映府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Xiao Ying, Marquis of Xinyü under Liang, was assigned to Guangzhou, Ke concurrently served as military attendant of Ying's princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang Marquis of Xinyü, Xiao Ying, went to Guangzhou, Shen Ke served concurrently as military attendant in Ying's princely household.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝與恪同郡，情好甚昵。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi and Ke were from the same commandery; their affection was very close.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi and Shen Ke were from the same commandery, and their friendship was unusually close.

sentences.zh: 蕭映卒後，武帝南討李賁，仍遣妻子附恪還鄉。

translations.literal: After Xiao Ying died, Chen Wudi marched south to attack Li Bin and sent his wife and children to join Ke and return to their home district.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Ying's death, as Chen Wudi marched south against Li Bin, he sent his wife and children to travel with Shen Ke back to their homeland.

sentences.zh: 尋補東宮直後。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Direct Attendant of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed direct attendant of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 以嶺南勳，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: For his merits in Lingnan, he was appointed Supernumerary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: For his services in Lingnan he was made supernumerary attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 仍令總集宗從子弟。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to gather and organize the clan cousins and younger kin.
translations.idiomatic: He was also charged with gathering and organizing the younger men of the clan.

sentences.zh: 侯景圍台城，起東西二土山以逼城，城內亦作土山應之，恪為東土山主，晝夜拒戰。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, he raised two earthen mounds east and west to press the city; within the city earthen mounds were likewise built to counter them. Ke served as commander of the eastern mound and fought off attacks day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, he raised earthen mounds east and west to press the walls; the defenders built counter-mounds within the city. Shen Ke commanded the eastern mound and fought without rest, day and night.

sentences.zh: 以功封東興侯。

translations.literal: For his merits he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was created Marquis of Dongxing.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，間行歸鄉。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he made his way home by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he stole his way home.

sentences.zh: 武帝討景，遣使報恪，恪於東起兵相應。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi attacked Hou Jing, he sent messengers to notify Ke, and Ke raised troops in the east in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi moved against Hou Jing, he sent word to Shen Ke, who raised forces in the east in answer.

sentences.zh: 賊平後，授都軍副。

translations.literal: After the rebels were suppressed, he was appointed Deputy Chief of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he was made deputy chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 及武帝謀討王僧辯，恪預其事。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi planned to attack Wang Sengbian, Ke took part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi plotted against Wang Sengbian, Shen Ke was party to the plan.

sentences.zh: 武帝使文帝還長城立柵備杜龕，使恪還武康招集兵眾。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to build palisades against Du Kan, and sent Ke back to Wukang to gather troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi sent Emperor Wen to Changcheng to erect palisades against Du Kan, and sent Shen Ke back to Wukang to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯誅，龕果遣副將杜泰襲文帝于長城，恪時已出縣，誅龕黨與。

translations.literal: When Sengbian was executed, Kan indeed sent his deputy Du Tai to surprise Emperor Wen at Changcheng. Ke had already left the county and executed Kan's associates.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian was killed, Du Kan did send his lieutenant Du Tai to strike at Emperor Wen in Changcheng. Shen Ke had already left the county and was executing Du Kan's partisans.

sentences.zh: 武帝尋遣周文育來援長城，文育至，泰乃走。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi soon sent Zhou Wenyü to reinforce Changcheng. When Wenyü arrived, Tai fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi soon dispatched Zhou Wenyü to relieve Changcheng; when Zhou Wenyü arrived, Du Tai withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及龕平，文帝襲東揚州刺史張彪，以恪監吳興郡。

translations.literal: When Kan was pacified, Emperor Wen attacked Zhang Biao, Governor of Eastern Yangzhou, and appointed Ke as overseer of Wuxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Du Kan was subdued, Emperor Wen struck at Zhang Biao, governor of Eastern Yangzhou, and put Shen Ke in charge of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，時恪自吳興入朝，武帝使中書舍人劉師知引恪，令勒兵入，因衛敬帝如別宮。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi accepted the abdication, Ke at the time had come from Wuxing to court. Chen Wudi had the Palace Secretariat Attendant Liu Shizhi bring Ke in, ordered him to lead troops inside, and thus escorted Emperor Jing to a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi accepted the abdication, Shen Ke had just arrived at court from Wuxing. The emperor had palace secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi conduct him in and ordered him to enter with troops and escort Emperor Jing to a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 恪排闥入見武帝，叩頭謝曰：「恪身經事蕭家來，今日不忍見此事，分受死耳，決不奉命。」

translations.literal: Ke pushed open the door and went in to see Chen Wudi. Prostrating himself he said in apology: "Ke has served the Xiao house all my life. Today I cannot bear to witness this affair. I merely ask to receive death—I will absolutely not obey the order."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ke pushed through the door to see Chen Wudi, kowtowed, and said, "I have served the house of Xiao all my days. I cannot bear to witness what is done today. Let me accept death—but I will not obey this command.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉其意，不復逼，更以蕩主王僧志代之。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi admired his intent and did not press him further; he had the garrison commander Wang Sengzhi take his place instead.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi admired his scruple and did not force him; he had the garrison commander Wang Sengzhi take his place instead.

sentences.zh: 帝踐阼，除吳興太守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, Ke was appointed Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: When the new emperor took the throne, Shen Ke was appointed governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 永定三年，除散騎常侍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongding, he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongding (559) he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 曆事文帝及廢帝，累遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Serving under Emperor Wen and Emperor Fei, he was promoted in succession to Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen and Emperor Fei he rose in due course to protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 至宣帝即位，除平越中郎將、都督、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan acceded, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Yue, Area Commander, and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Shen Ke was appointed general who pacifies the Yue, area commander, and governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恪未至嶺，前刺史歐陽紇舉兵拒嶮，不得進。

translations.literal: Before Ke reached the passes, the former governor Ouyang He raised troops and blocked the strategic passes; he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shen Ke had crossed the mountains, the former governor Ouyang He had risen in arms and held the passes, barring his advance.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣司空章昭達討平紇，乃得入州。

translations.literal: The court sent the Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda to suppress He, and only then was he able to enter the province.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent minister of works Zhang Zhaoda to put Ouyang He down, and only then could Shen Ke enter the province.

sentences.zh: 兵荒之後，所在殘毀，恪綏懷安輯，被以恩惠，嶺表賴之。

translations.literal: After the warfare and devastation, everywhere was in ruins. Ke soothed and settled the people, spreading favors upon them, and the region south of the passes relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of war and ruin the land lay wasted on every side. Shen Ke comforted and settled the people, showering them with kindness, and the whole region south of the passes looked to him for stability.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，為特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Houzhu acceded, Ke was made Special Court Advisor and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Houzhu succeeded, Shen Ke was made special court advisor and grand master of splendid virtue with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰光。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Guang ("Radiant").

sentences.zh: 子法興嗣。

translations.literal: His son Faxing succeeded to his title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Faxing inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 陸子隆字興世，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zilong, courtesy name Xingshi, was a native of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zilong, courtesy name Xingshi, was from Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖敞之，梁嘉興令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Changzhi was Magistrate of Jiaxing under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Changzhi had been magistrate of Jiaxing under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父悛，封氏令。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Magistrate of Fengshi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan was magistrate of Fengshi.

sentences.zh: 子隆少慷慨，有志功名。

translations.literal: Zilong was bold and open-hearted from youth and aspired to achievement and fame.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Lu Zilong was high-spirited and ambitious for honor and achievement.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，於鄉里聚徒。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, he gathered followers in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he gathered a band of followers in his home district.

sentences.zh: 時張彪為吳郡太守，引為將帥，仍隨彪徙鎮會稽。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Biao was Governor of Wu Commandery; he recruited Zilong as a commander, and Zilong followed Biao when he was transferred to garrison Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao was then governor of Wu; he took Lu Zilong into his service as a commander, and Lu Zilong followed him when he was reassigned to garrison Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 及文帝討彪，彪將沈泰、吳寶真、申縉等皆降，而子隆力戰敗績。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen attacked Biao, Biao's generals Shen Tai, Wu Baozhen, Shen Jin and others all surrendered, but Zilong fought hard and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen moved against Zhang Biao, Biao's generals Shen Tai, Wu Baozhen, Shen Jin, and the rest all surrendered—but Lu Zilong fought on stubbornly and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 文帝義之，復使領其部曲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen admired his sense of duty and again had him lead his own contingent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen respected his loyalty and restored him to command of his own troops.

sentences.zh: 文帝嗣位，子隆領甲仗宿衛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Zilong led the armor and weapons detail in palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Lu Zilong commanded the armory guard in palace service.

sentences.zh: 封益陽縣子，累遷廬陵太守。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yiyang and promoted in succession to Governor of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Viscount of Yiyang and later promoted to governor of Luling.

sentences.zh: 周迪據臨川反，子隆隨章昭達討迪，迪退走，因隨昭達討陳寶應。

translations.literal: Zhou Di held Linchuan and rebelled. Zilong followed Zhang Zhaoda to attack Di; Di retreated, and Zilong then followed Zhaoda to attack Chen Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Di seized Linchuan and rebelled, Lu Zilong marched with Zhang Zhaoda against him. After Zhou Di fled, Lu Zilong continued with Zhang Zhaoda to suppress Chen Baoying.

sentences.zh: 晉安平，子隆功最，遷武州刺史，改封朝陽縣伯。

translations.literal: When Jin'an was pacified, Zilong's achievements were greatest; he was transferred to Governor of Wuzhou and re-enfeoffed as Count of Chaoyang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin'an was pacified, Lu Zilong's merit stood highest. He was made governor of Wu and created Count of Chaoyang.

sentences.zh: 華皎據湘州反，以子隆居其心腹，皎深患之，頻遣使招，子隆不從，攻又不克。

translations.literal: Hua Jiao held Xiangzhou and rebelled. As Zilong was positioned in his very heartland, Jiao deeply feared him; he repeatedly sent envoys to recruit him, but Zilong would not join, and attacks against him could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao rebelled and held Xiangzhou. Lu Zilong sat deep in his rear, and Jiao feared him greatly—again and again he sent envoys to win him over, but Lu Zilong refused, and every attack on him failed.

sentences.zh: 及皎敗於郢州，子隆出兵襲其後，因與大軍相會。

translations.literal: When Jiao was defeated at Yingzhou, Zilong led troops out to strike his rear and thereby joined the main army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao was broken at Ying, Lu Zilong sallied forth to cut off his retreat and joined the main force.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯。

translations.literal: His noble rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 尋遷都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Area Commander and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made area commander and governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 荊州新置，居公安，城池未固，子隆修立城郭，綏集夷夏，甚得人和，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Jingzhou had been newly established, with its seat at Gong'an; the walls and moats were not yet secure. Zilong built up the city fortifications, soothed and gathered both barbarians and Chinese, greatly won popular harmony, and was called fully competent in his office.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was newly created, with its seat at Gong'an and its walls still unfinished. Lu Zilong rebuilt the defenses, pacified both barbarian and Chinese populations, and won such harmony that men said he filled the post as it ought to be filled.

sentences.zh: 吏人詣闕求立碑頌美功績，詔許之。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners went to the capital to request that a stele be erected praising his achievements; an edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people traveled to the capital to ask that a monument be raised in praise of his deeds, and the throne granted their request.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡威。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zilong died and was posthumously named Wei ("Formidable").

sentences.zh: 子之武嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhiwu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lu Zhiwu inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 之武年十六，領其舊軍。

translations.literal: Zhiwu was sixteen years old and took command of his father's former army.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Lu Zhiwu assumed command of his father's old troops.

sentences.zh: 後為弘農太守，乃隸吳明徹，于呂梁軍敗逃歸，為人所害。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of Hongnong, came under Wu Mingche's command, fled home after defeat at Luliang, and was killed by others.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Hongnong under Wu Mingche, fled home after the defeat at Luliang, and was murdered on the way.

sentences.zh: 子隆弟子才，亦有幹略。

translations.literal: Zilong's younger brother Zicai also had ability and strategic talent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zilong's younger brother Lu Zicai was likewise capable and shrewd in counsel.

sentences.zh: 從子隆征討有功，除始平太守，封始康縣子。

translations.literal: He followed Zilong on campaigns with merit, was appointed Governor of Shiping, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shikang County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Lu Zilong on campaign with distinction, was made governor of Shiping, and created Viscount of Shikang.

sentences.zh: 卒于信州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Governor of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as governor of Xin.

sentences.zh: 錢道戢字子韜，吳興長城人也。

translations.literal: Qian Daoji, courtesy name Zitao, was a native of Changcheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daoji, style name Zitao, came from Changcheng in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父景深，梁漢壽令。

translations.literal: His father Qian Jingshen was Magistrate of Hanshou under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian Jingshen had been magistrate of Hanshou under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 道戢少以孝行著聞，及長，頗有材幹，陳武帝微時，以從妹妻焉。

translations.literal: Daoji was known in youth for filial conduct; when grown he had considerable talent. When Chen Wudi was still obscure, Daoji gave him his cousin by marriage as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daoji won early fame for filial piety and, when grown, proved a man of real ability. In Chen Wudi's obscure days he gave the future emperor his cousin in marriage.

sentences.zh: 武帝輔政，道戢隨文帝平張彪於會稽，以功拜東徐州刺史，封永安縣侯。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi held the regency, Daoji followed Chen Wen to pacify Zhang Biao at Kuaiji; for his merit he was appointed Governor of East Xuzhou and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: While Chen Wudi held the regency, Qian Daoji marched with Chen Wen to crush Zhang Biao at Kuaiji and was rewarded with the governorship of East Xu and the marquisate of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，又隨昭達征江陵，以功加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian, he again followed Zhaoda in the campaign against Jiangling and was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taijian (574) he again followed Zhang Zhaoda against Jiangling and, for his services, was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後為都督、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Area Commander and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as area commander and governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 與儀同黃法奭攻下曆陽，因以道戢鎮之。

translations.literal: Together with Yitong Huang Fashi he captured Liyang, and Daoji was then stationed there to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: With the Yitong Huang Fashi he took Liyang, and Qian Daoji was left to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous title was Su.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his post and was posthumously named Su ("Solemn").

sentences.zh: 子邈嗣。

translations.literal: His son Miao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian Miao inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 駱文牙字旗門，吳興臨安人也。

translations.literal: Luo Wenya, courtesy name Qimen, was a native of Lin'an in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Wenya, style name Qimen, came from Lin'an in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父裕，梁鄱陽嗣王中兵參軍事。

translations.literal: His father Luo Yu was Central Army Aide-de-Camp to the Prince of Poyang under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luo Yu had been central army aide to the Prince of Poyang under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 文牙年十二，宗人有善相者，云：「此郎容貌非常，必將遠致。」

translations.literal: When Wenya was twelve, a clansman skilled in physiognomy said: "This young man's features are extraordinary; he will surely attain great things far and wide."
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, a kinsman versed in physiognomy told him: "This boy's face is unlike any other; he will rise to eminence far from home."

sentences.zh: 梁太清末，陳文帝避地臨安，文牙母陳，睹帝儀錶，知非常人，賓待甚厚。

translations.literal: At the end of the Liang Taqing era, Chen Wen took refuge in Lin'an. Wenya's mother, née Chen, saw the emperor's bearing, knew he was no ordinary man, and entertained him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Liang Taqing, Chen Wen took refuge at Lin'an. Wenya's mother, Lady Chen, read the future emperor's bearing, knew he was no common man, and received him with lavish hospitality.

sentences.zh: 及帝為吳興太守，引文牙為將帥。

translations.literal: When the emperor became Governor of Wuxing, he brought Wenya in as a military commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wen became governor of Wuxing, he took Luo Wenya into his command as a field officer.

sentences.zh: 從平杜龕、張彪，勇冠眾軍。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Du Kan and Zhang Biao; his courage surpassed all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the campaigns against Du Kan and Zhang Biao, and his valor outshone every other unit.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，封臨安縣侯，位越州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chen Wen came to the throne, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Lin'an County and appointed Governor of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wen succeeded to the throne, Luo Wenya was created Marquis of Lin'an and made governor of Yue.

sentences.zh: 初，文牙母卒，時兵荒，至是始葬，詔贈臨安國太夫人，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Earlier Wenya's mother had died during the turmoil of war, and only now was she finally buried. An edict posthumously granted her the title Grand Lady of Lin'an State, with posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had died amid the chaos of war and could be buried only now; the court posthumously ennobled her as Grand Lady of Lin'an State with the posthumous name Gong ("Respectful").

sentences.zh: 太建八年，文牙累遷散騎常侍，入直殿省。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian, Wenya was promoted in succession to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and entered palace duty in the Hall Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taijian (580) Luo Wenya rose to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and entered service in the palace directorate.

sentences.zh: 十年，授豐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Governor of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed governor of Feng.

sentences.zh: 至德二年卒，贈廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Zhide, and was posthumously granted the post of Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhide (584) and was posthumously made governor of Guang.

sentences.zh: 子義嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luo Yi inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 孫瑒字德璉，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Sun Yang, courtesy name Delian, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yang, style name Delian, came from Wu in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父修道，梁中散大夫，以雅素知名。

translations.literal: His father Sun Xiudao was Palace Attendant under the Liang, renowned for refined simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Xiudao had been a palace attendant under the Liang, famed for unpretentious elegance.

sentences.zh: 瑒少倜儻，好謀略，博涉經史，尤便書翰。

translations.literal: Yang in youth was bold and free-spirited, fond of strategy, broadly versed in the classics and histories, and especially skilled at calligraphy and correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yang was dashing and open-handed from youth, loved stratagem, read widely in the classics and histories, and was especially accomplished at brush and letter.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為邵陵王中兵參軍事。

translations.literal: Under the Liang he served as Central Army Aide-de-Camp to the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as central army aide to the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 太清之難，授假節、宣猛將軍、軍主。

translations.literal: During the Taqing crisis he was granted provisional authority, the title General Who Proclaims Fierceness, and command of an army detachment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taqing crisis he received provisional credentials, the title general who proclaims fierceness, and an independent command.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯之討侯景也，王琳為前軍，琳與瑒親婭，乃表薦為宜都太守。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Wang Lin led the vanguard. Lin and Yang were related by marriage, and Lin memorialized recommending Yang as Governor of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian marched against Hou Jing, Wang Lin commanded the vanguard. Lin and Sun Yang were kin by marriage, and Lin memorialized to have Sun Yang appointed governor of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功封富陽侯。

translations.literal: Later for military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: For later military service he was created Marquis of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 敬帝立，累遷巴州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, he was promoted in succession to Governor of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing succeeded, Sun Yang rose in due course to governor of Ba.

sentences.zh: 及陳武帝受禪，王琳立梁永嘉王蕭莊於郢州，征瑒為少府卿，仍徙都督、郢州刺史，總留府之任。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi accepted the abdication, Wang Lin set up Xiao Zhuang, Prince of Yongjia of Liang, at Yingzhou. Yang was summoned as Minister of the Palace Storehouse, then transferred to Area Commander and Governor of Yingzhou, assuming overall charge of affairs left at the seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi took the throne, Wang Lin installed Xiao Zhuang, the Liang Prince of Yongjia, at Ying. Sun Yang was summoned as minister of the palace storehouse, then made area commander and governor of Ying with full charge of the seat left behind.

sentences.zh: 周遣大將軍史甯乘虛攻之，瑒兵不滿千人，乘城拒守，周兵不能克。

translations.literal: Zhou sent the great general Shi Ning to attack while the opportunity was open. Yang's troops numbered fewer than a thousand; he mounted the walls to resist, and the Zhou army could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou sent the great general Shi Ning to strike while the city was exposed. Sun Yang had fewer than a thousand men, yet held the walls and kept the Zhou army at bay.

sentences.zh: 及聞大軍敗王琳，乘勝而進，周兵乃解，瑒於是盡有中流之地。

translations.literal: When word came that the main army had defeated Wang Lin and was pressing forward in victory, the Zhou troops withdrew, and Yang then held the entire midstream region.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived that the main force had broken Wang Lin and was advancing in triumph, the Zhou troops lifted the siege, and Sun Yang came to hold the whole mid-Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 既而遣使奉表歸陳。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he sent envoys with a memorial submitting to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent envoys with a memorial of submission to Chen.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，授湘州刺史，封定襄縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, he was appointed Governor of Xiangzhou and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was made governor of Xiang and created Marquis of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 瑒懷不自安，乃固請入朝，徵為侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Yang felt ill at ease and firmly requested to come to court; he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his post, Sun Yang repeatedly asked to come to court and was recalled as palace attendant and general who leads the army.

sentences.zh: 未拜，文帝謂曰：「昔朱買臣願為本郡，卿豈有意乎？」

translations.literal: Before he could take office, Chen Wen said to him: "Long ago Zhu Maichen wished to serve as governor of his home commandery—do you have such a wish?"
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post, Chen Wen asked him: "Zhu Maichen once longed to govern his home commandery—do you feel the same?"

sentences.zh: 改授吳郡太守，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was instead appointed Governor of Wu Commandery and granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he was appointed governor of Wu Commandery and granted a full set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，徵拜散騎常侍、中護軍。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was summoned and appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Central Army Protector.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was recalled as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and central army protector.

sentences.zh: 及留異反，據東陽，詔瑒督舟師進討。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi rebelled and held Dongyang, an edict ordered Yang to command the fleet and advance to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi rebelled and seized Dongyang, an edict put Sun Yang in command of the river fleet to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 異平，遷鎮右將軍。

translations.literal: When Yi was pacified, he was transferred to General Who Guards the Right.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yi was crushed, Sun Yang was made general who guards the right.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出為建安太守。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Governor of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as governor of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，為都督、荊州刺史，出鎮公安，為鄰境所憚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian, he served as Area Commander and Governor of Jingzhou, going out to garrison Gong'an; neighboring territories feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taijian (576) he became area commander and governor of Jing, took up his post at Gong'an, and was feared by every neighboring command.

sentences.zh: 居職六年，以公事免。

translations.literal: After six years in office he was dismissed on account of official business.
translations.idiomatic: Six years into the post he was removed for an official offense.

sentences.zh: 及吳明徹軍敗呂梁，詔授都督緣江水陸諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche's army was defeated at Luliang, an edict appointed him Area Commander over all land and water forces along the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Mingche's defeat at Luliang, an edict made Sun Yang area commander of all land and river forces along the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 尋授都督、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Area Commander and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the joint posts of area commander and governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 十二年，坐疆埸交通抵罪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was convicted for illicit contact across the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was punished for unauthorized dealings across the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，復爵邑。

translations.literal: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne, his title and fief were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu came to the throne, Sun Yang's title and fief were restored.

sentences.zh: 歷位度支尚書，侍中，祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister of Revenue, Palace Attendant, and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as minister of revenue, palace attendant, and minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 後主頻幸其宅，賦詩述勳德之美。

translations.literal: Houzhu often visited his residence and composed poetry describing the beauty of his achievements and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu often visited his house and wrote poems praising his merit and character.

sentences.zh: 遷五兵尚書，領左軍將軍，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War, concurrently General of the Left Army, while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to minister of war and general of the left army while keeping his palace attendant's seat.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年，卒官，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, he died in office; his posthumous title was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenming (587) he died in office and was posthumously named Huan ("Constant").

sentences.zh: 瑒事親以孝聞，于諸弟甚篤睦。

translations.literal: Yang was known for filial service to his parents and was deeply harmonious with his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yang was famed for filial devotion to his parents and for warm, steadfast affection among his brothers.

sentences.zh: 性通泰，有財散之親友。

translations.literal: By nature he was open and easy; whenever he had wealth he distributed it among friends and kin.
translations.idiomatic: Open-handed by temperament, he gave freely to friends and kin whenever fortune came his way.

sentences.zh: 居家頗失於侈，家庭穿築，極林泉之致，歌鍾舞女，當世罕儔。

translations.literal: At home he was rather extravagant: he dug and built throughout the household estate to the utmost charm of woods and springs, with singing bells and dancing girls rarely matched in his age.
translations.idiomatic: His household was lavish beyond measure: he excavated ponds and terraces until the grounds rivaled the finest groves and streams, and kept singers, bells, and dancing girls such as few men of the age could equal.

sentences.zh: 賓客填門，軒蓋不絕。

translations.literal: Guests filled his gate; carriages with canopies never ceased arriving.
translations.idiomatic: Guests packed his gate, and covered carriages streamed in without pause.

sentences.zh: 及出鎮郢州，乃合十餘船為大舫，于中立亭池，植荷芰，每良辰美景，賓僚並集，泛長江而置酒，亦一時之勝賞焉。

translations.literal: When he went out to garrison Yingzhou, he joined more than ten boats into a great pleasure barge, built a pavilion and pond in its midst, and planted lotus and water chestnuts. On every fine day and lovely scene, guests and subordinates would gather, float wine on the Yangtze, and enjoy one of the age's supreme delights.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out to hold Ying, he lashed a dozen boats into one great pleasure craft, set a pavilion and pool in its center, and planted lotus and water caltrop. On bright days he would gather guests and staff, drift down the Yangtze with wine cups set out, and savor one of the age's finest pleasures.

sentences.zh: 常於山齋設講肆，集玄儒之士，冬夏資奉，為學者所稱。

translations.literal: He often set up lecture halls in his mountain studio, gathering masters of the profound and Confucian learning, supporting them through winter and summer—a practice praised by scholars.
