translations.idiomatic: In his mountain retreat he often opened lecture halls for masters of Buddhist and Confucian learning, supporting them winter and summer—a generosity scholars widely praised.

sentences.zh: 而處己率易，不以名位驕物。

translations.literal: Yet in his personal conduct he was straightforward and easy, not arrogant toward others on account of rank and status.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his own bearing he was plain and unassuming, never haughty toward others because of rank.

sentences.zh: 時興皇寺慧朗法師該通釋典，瑒每造講筵，時有抗論，法侶莫不傾心。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Huilang of Xinghuang Temple was thoroughly versed in Buddhist scriptures. Yang often visited his lecture hall and sometimes engaged in spirited debate; none among the Buddhist community failed to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huilang of Xinghuang Temple was then master of the Buddhist canon. Sun Yang often attended his lectures and sometimes argued pointedly with him; the whole Buddhist community admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 又巧思過人，為起部尚書，軍國器械，多所創立。

translations.literal: He was also ingenious beyond others; as Minister of Works he created many new designs for military and state equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He was also inventive beyond his peers; as minister of works he devised many new instruments of war and state.

sentences.zh: 有鑒識，男女婚姻，皆擇素貴。

translations.literal: He had discerning judgment; for the marriages of sons and daughters he always chose families of plain virtue and high standing.
translations.idiomatic: He chose his children's spouses with care, always matching them to families of modest virtue and distinguished lineage.

sentences.zh: 及卒，尚書令江總為之銘志，後主又題銘後四十字，遣左戶尚書蔡征就宅宣敕鐫之。

translations.literal: When he died, Chief Minister Jiang Zong composed his epitaph inscription. Houzhu added forty characters after the inscription and sent Left Minister of the Household Cai Zheng to his residence to proclaim the edict and have it carved.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Chief Minister Jiang Zong wrote his epitaph. Houzhu appended forty characters of his own and sent Left Minister of the Household Cai Zheng to the house to proclaim the edict and have the text cut in stone.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：「秋風動竹，煙水驚波。

translations.literal: The text reads: "Autumn wind stirs the bamboo; misty waters startle the waves.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription runs: "Autumn wind shakes the bamboo; mist over the water ruffles the waves.

sentences.zh: 幾人樵徑，何處山阿。

translations.literal: How many now tread the woodcutters' paths? Where are the mountain glens?
translations.idiomatic: Who still walks the woodcutters' trail? Where now the hidden hill?

sentences.zh: 今時日月，宿昔綺羅。

translations.literal: Today's sun and moon—yesterday's silks and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon are still here; the silks and brocades are gone.

sentences.zh: 天長路遠，地久靈多。

translations.literal: Heaven is long, the road far; earth endures, the spirit manifold.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven stretches on, the road runs far; earth endures, and the spirit abides in many forms.

sentences.zh: 功臣未勒，此意如何。」

translations.literal: Meritorious deeds uncarved in stone—what meaning in this thought?"
translations.idiomatic: His merit uncarved on stone—what can this sorrow mean?"

sentences.zh: 時論以為榮。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held this an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time counted it a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 瑒二十一子，第二子訓頗知名，位高唐太守，陳亡入隋。

translations.literal: Yang had twenty-one sons; his second son Xun was quite renowned, served as Governor of Gaotang, and entered the Sui when Chen fell.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yang had twenty-one sons; the second, Xun, was well known, served as governor of Gaotang, and passed into the Sui when Chen fell.

sentences.zh: 徐世譜字興宗，巴東魚復人也。

translations.literal: Xu Shipu, courtesy name Xingzong, was a native of Yufu in Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shipu, style name Xingzong, came from Yufu in Badong.

sentences.zh: 世居荊州為主帥，征伐蠻蜒。

translations.literal: His family for generations lived in Jingzhou as local commanders, campaigning against the Man and Yan tribes.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his clan had served in Jing as local commanders, campaigning against the Man and Yan peoples.

sentences.zh: 至世譜尤勇敢，有膂力，善水戰。

translations.literal: By Shipu's time he was especially brave, possessed great physical strength, and excelled at naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: In Xu Shipu's day he was outstandingly bold, powerfully built, and masterful on the water.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝之為荊州刺史，世譜將領鄉人事焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was Governor of Jingzhou, Shipu led the township militia in his service.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was governor of Jing, Xu Shipu led the local militia in his service.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，因預征討，累遷至員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he took part in the campaigns and rose in succession to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he joined the campaigns and rose in due course to supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋領水軍，從司徒陸法和與景戰於赤亭湖。

translations.literal: Soon he commanded the navy, following Marshal Lu Fahe in battle against Jing at Chiting Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took command of the river force and, under Marshal Lu Fahe, fought Hou Jing at Chiting Lake.

sentences.zh: 時景軍甚盛，世譜乃別造樓船、拍艦、火舫、水車以益軍勢。

translations.literal: At the time Jing's army was very strong; Shipu then specially built tower ships, ram ships, fire boats, and water chariots to augment military power.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's fleet was then at its height; Xu Shipu built tower ships, rams, fire boats, and water chariots to strengthen his own force.

sentences.zh: 將戰，又乘大艦居前，大敗景軍，禽景將任約。

translations.literal: As battle was about to begin, he again rode a great ship to the fore, utterly routed Jing's army, and captured Jing's general Ren Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When battle opened he again took the lead in a great ship, broke Hou Jing's army, and captured his general Ren Yue.

sentences.zh: 景退走，因隨王僧辯攻郢州，世譜復乘大艦臨其倉門，賊將宋子仙據城降。

translations.literal: Jing retreated and fled; Shipu then followed Wang Sengbian in the attack on Yingzhou. Shipu again rode a great ship up to the granary gate; the rebel general Song Zixian held the city and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing fled; Xu Shipu then followed Wang Sengbian against Ying, again driving a great ship to the granary gate until the rebel Song Zixian, holding the city, submitted.

sentences.zh: 以功除信州刺史，封魚復縣侯。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Governor of Xinzhou and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yufu County.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made governor of Xin and created Marquis of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 仍隨僧辯東下，恒為軍鋒。

translations.literal: He continued following Sengbian eastward and was constantly the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He continued east with Wang Sengbian and was always at the army's spearhead.

sentences.zh: 景平，以衡州刺史資，領河東太守。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, with the salary of Governor of Hengzhou he concurrently served as Governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat he drew the emoluments of governor of Heng while serving concurrently as governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 西魏攻荊州，世譜鎮馬頭岸，據有龍洲。

translations.literal: When Western Wei attacked Jingzhou, Shipu garrisoned Matou Bank and held Long Island.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei attacked Jing, Xu Shipu held Matou Bank and seized Long Island.

sentences.zh: 元帝授侍中、都督江南諸軍事、鎮南將軍、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him Palace Attendant, Area Commander over all forces south of the Yangtze, General Who Guards the South, and Army Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan made him palace attendant, area commander of all forces south of the Yangtze, general who guards the south, and army protector.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，世譜東下依侯瑱。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, Shipu went east and attached himself to Hou Tian.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling, Xu Shipu went east and placed himself under Hou Tian.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding, he was transferred to Army Protector.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongding (558) he was made army protector.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，曆特進、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Chen Wen came to the throne, he successively held the posts of Special Advisor and Right Grand Master for Splendor and Wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wen succeeded, Xu Shipu served in turn as special advisor and right grand master for splendor and wealth.

sentences.zh: 以疾失明，謝病不朝。

translations.literal: Illness robbed him of sight; he resigned on grounds of illness and ceased attending court.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness took his sight; he pleaded illness and withdrew from court.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Huan ("Constant").

sentences.zh: 周敷字仲遠，臨川人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, style name Zhongyuan, came from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 為郡豪族。

translations.literal: His family were a powerful clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was one of the great magnate families of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 敷形貌眇小，如不勝衣，膽力勁果，超出時輩。

translations.literal: Fu's physique was small and slight, as if unable to bear his clothes, yet his courage and resolve were fierce and resolute, surpassing men of his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu was slight of build, as though his frame could barely fill his robes, yet his courage and resolution were iron-hard and outstripped his peers.

sentences.zh: 性豪俠，輕財重士，鄉党少年任氣者咸歸之。

translations.literal: By nature he was chivalrous and bold, lightly esteeming wealth and heavily esteeming men of talent; young men in the district who lived by their pride all rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chivalrous by nature, he scorned money and honored men of spirit; every hot-blooded youth in the district rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，鄉人周續合眾以討賊為事，梁內史始興蕃王蕭毅以郡讓續，續所部有欲侵掠毅者，敷擁護之，親率其黨，捍送至豫章。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, his townsman Zhou Xu gathered a host to make suppressing the rebels their task. Xiao Yi, Prince of Shixing, Interior Minister of Liang, ceded the commandery to Xu. Among Xu's subordinates were some who wished to plunder Yi; Fu protected him, personally leading his band to escort him safely to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion his townsman Zhou Xu raised a force to fight the rebels. Xiao Yi, Prince of Shixing and interior minister of Liang, yielded the commandery to Xu. When some of Xu's men meant to plunder the prince, Zhou Fu shielded him and personally led his followers to escort him safely to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 時梁觀甯侯蕭永、長樂侯蕭基、豐城侯蕭泰避難流寓，聞敷信義，皆往依之。

translations.literal: At the time, Liang's Marquis Guanning Xiao Yong, Marquis Changle Xiao Ji, and Marquis Fengcheng Xiao Tai, refugees in flight, heard of Fu's integrity and trustworthiness and all went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liang nobles—the Marquises Guanning, Changle, and Fengcheng, Xiao Yong, Xiao Ji, and Xiao Tai—were living in exile as refugees. Hearing of Zhou Fu's reputation for honor, they all came to place themselves under his protection.

sentences.zh: 敷湣其危懼，屈體崇敬，厚加給恤，送之西上。

translations.literal: Fu pitied their peril and fear, humbled himself in reverent respect, generously provided relief and care, and sent them westward.
translations.idiomatic: Fu took pity on their terror and distress, bowed to them in respectful courtesy, lavished gifts and support upon them, and escorted them on their journey west.

sentences.zh: 俄而續部下將帥爭權，殺續以降周迪。

translations.literal: Before long, generals under Xu fought over power, killed Xu, and submitted to Zhou Di.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xu's subordinate commanders quarreled over authority, murdered Xu, and surrendered to Zhou Di.

sentences.zh: 迪素無簿閥，又失眾心，倚敷族望，深求交結。

translations.literal: Di by nature had no pedigree in the registers, and again had lost popular support; relying on Fu's clan prestige, he sought alliance deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Di came from no distinguished lineage and had already lost the hearts of his men. He leaned on Fu's family standing and pressed hard for an alliance.

sentences.zh: 敷未能自固，事迪甚恭，迪大憑仗之。

translations.literal: Fu could not yet secure himself and served Di with great deference; Di relied heavily on him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had not yet consolidated his own position and treated Di with elaborate deference; Di in turn leaned on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 迪據臨川之工塘，敷鎮臨川故郡。

translations.literal: Di held Gongtang in Linchuan; Fu garrisoned the former Linchuan commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: Di occupied Gongtang in Linchuan, while Fu held the old Linchuan commandery capital.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，梁元帝授敷甯州刺史，封西豐縣侯。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Fu Governor of Ningzhou and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat, Emperor Yuan of Liang made Fu governor of Ning and created him Marquis of Xifeng.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，王琳據有上流，余孝頃與琳党李孝欽等共圍周迪，敷助於迪，迪禽孝頃等，敷功最多。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi received the abdication, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Yu Xiaqing together with Wang Lin's partisan Li Xiaoqin and others jointly besieged Zhou Di. Fu assisted Di; Di captured Xiaqing and the others, and Fu's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi took the throne, Wang Lin controlled the upper Yangzi. Yu Xiaqing joined Wang Lin's ally Li Xiaoqin and others in besieging Zhou Di. Fu fought on Di's side; when Di captured Xiaqing and his fellows, Fu's contribution was the greatest of all.

sentences.zh: 熊曇朗之殺周文育，據豫章，將兵襲敷，敷大破之。

translations.literal: After Xiong Tanlang killed Zhou Wenyü and seized Yuzhang, he led troops to raid Fu, and Fu routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiong Tanlang murdered Zhou Wenyü and seized Yuzhang, he marched against Fu with an army. Fu crushed him completely.

sentences.zh: 曇朗走巴山郡，敷因與周迪、黃法奭等進兵屠之。

translations.literal: Tanlang fled to Bashan commandery; Fu thereupon joined Zhou Di, Huang Fashi, and others in advancing to slaughter him.
translations.idiomatic: Tanlang fled to Bashan commandery. Fu then joined Zhou Di, Huang Fashi, and others in a punitive advance that wiped him out.

sentences.zh: 王琳平，授散騎常侍、豫章太守。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was pacified, [Fu] was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin's defeat, Fu was appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 時南江酋帥，並顧戀巢窟，唯敷獨先入朝。

translations.literal: At the time the chieftains of the southern rivers all clung to their native lairs; only Fu alone went first to court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the tribal leaders of the southern Yangzi country all clung to their home strongholds; Fu alone was the first to come to court.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，詣闕，進號安西將軍，令還鎮豫章。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, he came to the imperial audience, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West, and was ordered to return and garrison Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng he appeared at court, was promoted to general who pacifies the west, and was ordered back to garrison Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 周迪以敷素出己下，超致顯達，深不平，乃舉兵反，遣弟方興襲敷，敷大破之。

translations.literal: Zhou Di, because Fu had originally been beneath him yet had risen to prominence beyond expectation, was deeply resentful; he thereupon raised troops in rebellion and sent his younger brother Fangxing to raid Fu, but Fu routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Di resented Fu bitterly: Fu had once ranked below him, yet had risen to eminence far beyond his own. He raised troops in revolt and sent his brother Fangxing to attack Fu, but Fu routed the assault.

sentences.zh: 仍從都督吳明徹攻破迪，禽方興。

translations.literal: He then followed the Area Commander Wu Mingche in defeating Di and capturing Fangxing.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the area commander Wu Mingche in breaking Di's forces and capturing Fangxing.

sentences.zh: 再遷都督、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Area Commander and Governor of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to area commander and governor of South Yu.

sentences.zh: 迪又收餘眾襲東興，文帝遣都督章昭達征迪，敷又從軍。

translations.literal: Di again gathered remnant forces and raided Dongxing; Chen Wen dispatched Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to campaign against Di, and Fu again followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Di rallied his scattered troops and struck at Dongxing. Chen Wen sent the area commander Zhang Zhaoda against him, and Fu once more joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 至定川縣與迪相對，迪紿敷求還朝，欲立盟，敷許之。

translations.literal: Reaching Dingchuan county he confronted Di; Di deceived Fu with a request to return to court, wishing to establish an alliance, and Fu consented.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingchuan county he faced Di across the field. Di tricked him with a plea to return to court and a proposal to swear alliance. Fu agreed.

sentences.zh: 方登壇，為迪所害。

translations.literal: Just as he was mounting the altar, he was killed by Di.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely stepped onto the oath altar when Di killed him.

sentences.zh: 諡曰脫。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Tuo.

sentences.zh: 子智安嗣，位至太僕卿。

translations.literal: His son Zhian succeeded him and rose to the post of Master of Horse.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhian inherited his title and eventually reached the office of master of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 荀朗字深明，潁川潁陰人也。

translations.literal: Xun Lang, courtesy name Shenming, was a native of Yingyin in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Lang, styled Shenming, came from Yingyin in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖延祖，梁潁川太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanzu was Liang's Governor of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanzu had served Liang as governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父伯道，衛尉卿。

translations.literal: His father Bodao was Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bodao held the post of commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 朗少慷慨，有將帥大略。

translations.literal: Lang from youth was bold and open-handed and had the broad strokes of a general.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Lang was high-spirited and generous, with the makings of a field commander.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，據巢湖，無所屬。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he held Chaohu Lake and belonged to no faction.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he held the Chaohu region and owed allegiance to no one.

sentences.zh: 台城陷沒後，梁簡文帝密詔授朗豫州刺史，令與外蕃討景。

translations.literal: After the capital fell, Emperor Jian of Liang secretly issued an edict appointing Lang Governor of Yuzhou, ordering him to join the outer fiefs in campaigning against Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell, Emperor Jian of Liang sent a secret edict making Lang governor of Yu and ordering him to join the frontier lords in the campaign against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 景使儀同宋子仙、任約等頻征之，不能克。

translations.literal: Jing sent Commissioners-in-chief Song Zixian, Ren Yue, and others repeatedly to campaign against him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing dispatched the commissioners-in-chief Song Zixian, Ren Yue, and others against him again and again, but none could defeat him.

sentences.zh: 時都下饑，朗更招致部曲，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: At the time the capital district suffered famine; Lang further recruited retainers, and his forces reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the capital region. Lang kept recruiting followers until his command numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 侯景敗于巴陵，朗截破其後軍。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was defeated at Baling, Lang cut off and routed his rear army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was beaten at Baling, Lang fell upon his rear guard and shattered it.

sentences.zh: 景平後，又別破齊將郭元建於踟躕山。

translations.literal: After Jing was pacified, he separately defeated Northern Qi's general Guo Yuanjian at Mount Chizhu.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat he won a separate victory over Northern Qi's general Guo Yuanjian at Mount Chizhu.

sentences.zh: 及魏克荊州，陳武帝入輔，齊遣蕭軌、東方老等來寇，據石頭，朗自宣城來赴，與侯安都等大破之。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jingzhou and Chen Wudi entered the capital as regent, Qi sent Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, and others to raid; they seized Stone City. Lang came from Xuancheng to the rescue and, together with Hou Andu and others, routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jingzhou and Chen Wudi entered the capital as regent, Northern Qi sent Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, and others to invade and seized Stone City. Lang marched from Xuancheng to the relief and, with Hou Andu and the rest, inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 法尚少俶儻，有文武幹略。

translations.literal: Fashang from youth was free-spirited and unconstrained and possessed both civil and martial talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang was from youth bold and unbounded in spirit, with talent and capacity for both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 禎明中，為都督、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhenming he served as Area Commander and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenming era of Chen Houzhu he served as area commander and governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 及隋軍濟江，法尚降。

translations.literal: When Sui armies crossed the Yangzi, Fashang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui armies crossed the Yangzi, Fashang submitted.

sentences.zh: 入隋，曆邵、觀、綿、豐四州刺史，巴東、敦煌二郡太守。

translations.literal: Entering Sui, he successively served as Governor of Shao, Guan, Mian, and Feng prefectures and as Administrator of Badong and Dunhuang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served in turn as governor of Shao, Guan, Mian, and Feng and as administrator of Badong and Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 周炅字文昭，汝南安成人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Jiong, courtesy name Wenzhao, was a native of Ancheng in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jiong, styled Wenzhao, came from Ancheng in Runan.

sentences.zh: 祖強，齊梁州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiang was Liangzhou Governor under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiang had been Liangzhou governor under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父靈起，梁廬、桂二州刺史，保城縣侯。

translations.literal: His father Lingqi was Liang's Governor of Lu and Gui and Marquis of Baocheng County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingqi had served Liang as governor of Lu and Gui and held the title Marquis of Baocheng.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，為都督、安州刺史，改封龍源縣侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, he was made Area Commander and Governor of Anzhou and was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Longyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian of Chen Xuan he was appointed area commander and governor of An and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Longyuan.

sentences.zh: 其年，隨都督吳明徹北討，所向克捷，一月之中，獲十二城。

translations.literal: That same year he followed Area Commander Wu Mingche on the northern campaign; wherever they went they succeeded, and within one month they took twelve cities.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he joined the area commander Wu Mingche on the northern expedition. Wherever they turned they prevailed, and within a single month they captured twelve cities.

sentences.zh: 敗齊尚書左丞陸騫軍。

translations.literal: He defeated the army of Lu Qian, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the forces of Lu Qian, Northern Qi's left assistant director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 進攻巴州，克之。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Bazhou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on Ba prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 於是江北諸城及谷陽土人，並誅其渠帥以城降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the cities north of the Yangzi and the local strongmen of Guyang all executed their leaders and surrendered their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the cities north of the Yangzi and the local chiefs of Guyang all killed their headmen and surrendered their towns.

sentences.zh: 進號和戎將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Harmonizes with the Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who harmonizes with the Rong.

sentences.zh: 仍敕追炅入朝。

translations.literal: He was then ordered by imperial command to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order then recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 後梁定州刺史田龍升以城降，詔以為定州刺史，封赤亭王。

translations.literal: The Later Liang Governor of Dingzhou Tian Longsheng surrendered his city; an edict appointed him Governor of Dingzhou and created him Prince of Chiting.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Longsheng, governor of Ding under Later Liang, surrendered his city. The court appointed him governor of Ding and created him Prince of Chiting.

sentences.zh: 及炅入朝，龍升以江北六州七鎮叛入于齊，齊遣曆陽王高景安應之。

translations.literal: When Jiong came to court, Longsheng rebelled with six prefectures and seven garrisons north of the Yangzi and went over to Qi; Qi sent the Prince of Liyang Gao Jingan to support him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong arrived at court, Longsheng rebelled with six prefectures and seven garrisons north of the Yangzi and defected to Northern Qi. Qi sent the Prince of Liyang, Gao Jingan, to his aid.

sentences.zh: 於是令炅為江北道大都督，總統眾軍以討龍升，斬之，盡復江北之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiong was made Grand Area Commander of the Jiangbei circuit, commanding all armies to campaign against Longsheng; he beheaded him and fully recovered the lands north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was then made grand area commander of the Jiangbei circuit, leading all forces against Longsheng. He beheaded Longsheng and fully restored the territory north of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 進號平北將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，贈司州刺史，改封武昌郡公，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously he was made Governor of Sizhou, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Wuchang commandery, with the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. Posthumously he was made governor of Si, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Wuchang, and given the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 魯悉達字志通，扶風郿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Xida, courtesy name Zhitong, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xida, styled Zhitong, came from Mei in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 祖斐，齊衡州刺史、陽塘侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fei was Governor of Hengzhou under Qi and Marquis of Yangtang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fei had been Hengzhou governor under Northern Qi and Marquis of Yangtang.

sentences.zh: 父益之，梁雲麾將軍、新蔡義陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Yizhi was Liang's General of the Cloudy Pennant and Administrator of the two commanderies of Xincai and Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yizhi had served Liang as general of the cloudy pennant and administrator of Xincai and Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 悉達幼以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xida from childhood was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Xida was famed for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，糾合鄉人保新蔡，力田蓄穀。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he rallied fellow townsmen to hold Xincai, farming strenuously and storing grain.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he gathered his neighbors to defend Xincai, working the fields hard and hoarding grain.

sentences.zh: 時兵荒，都下及上川餓死者十八九，有得存者，皆攜老幼以歸焉，悉達所濟活者甚眾。

translations.literal: At the time of military chaos and famine, eight or nine out of ten in the capital region and the upper rivers died of hunger; those who survived all brought old and young home to him, and the number Xida saved was very great.
translations.idiomatic: War and famine raged; eight or nine in ten around the capital and upriver starved to death. Those who lived came trailing the old and the young to his gates, and the lives he saved were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 招集晉熙等五郡，盡有其地。

translations.literal: He gathered Jinxi and four other commanderies and wholly possessed their territories.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Jinxi and four neighboring commanderies under his sway until he held the whole region.

sentences.zh: 使其弟廣達領兵隨王僧辯討平侯景。

translations.literal: He had his younger brother Guangda lead troops to follow Wang Sengbian in pacifying Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his younger brother Guangda at the head of troops to join Wang Sengbian in the campaign that brought down Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝授北江州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him Governor of North Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him governor of North Jiang.

sentences.zh: 悉達雖仗氣任俠，不以富貴驕人。

translations.literal: Though Xida relied on force and practiced knight-errantry, he did not treat others arrogantly once rich and honored.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xida was proud and lived by the code of the sword, wealth and rank never made him condescend to others.

sentences.zh: 雅好詞賦，招禮賢才，與之賞會。

translations.literal: He was fond of poetry and rhapsodies, invited and honored men of talent, and joined them in literary gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: He loved poetry and rhapsody, welcomed scholars of talent, and shared literary gatherings with them.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，遷吳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chen Wen took the throne, [Xida] was transferred to Governor of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wen came to the throne, Xida was transferred to governor of Wu.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，哀毀過禮，因遘疾卒，諡孝侯。

translations.literal: Mourning his mother, his grief exceeded the rites and he fell ill and died; his posthumous title was Marquis Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned beyond what the rites allowed, fell ill, and passed away. He was posthumously titled Marquis Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子覽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Lan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 弟廣達。

translations.literal: Younger brother Guangda.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Guangda.

sentences.zh: 廣達字遍覽，少慷慨，志立功名，虛心愛士，賓客自遠而至。

translations.literal: Guangda, courtesy name Bianlan, from youth was bold and open-handed, resolved to establish merit and fame; open-hearted and fond of scholars, guests came to him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Guangda, styled Bianlan, was from youth ardent and generous, bent on winning glory in service. Humble before men of worth, he drew guests from distant places to his door.

sentences.zh: 時江表將帥各領部曲，動以千數，而魯氏尤為多。

translations.literal: At the time the generals south of the Yangzi each commanded retainers numbering in the thousands, and the Lu clan was especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In those days every commander south of the Yangzi led private followings counted in the thousands, and none was more numerous than the Lu family.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為平南當陽公府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Serving Liang, he was Army Staff Officer in the headquarters of the Prince of Dangyang, Pacifier of the South.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as army staff officer in the headquarters of the Prince of Dangyang, pacifier of the south.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，與兄悉達聚眾保新蔡。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he joined his elder brother Xida in gathering forces to hold Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he and his elder brother Xida raised troops to defend Xincai.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制授晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting under regency authority, appointed him Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang, exercising regency powers, appointed him governor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯之討侯景，廣達出境候接，資奉軍儲。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Guangda went beyond the border to meet and welcome him, supplying provisions for the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian marched against Hou Jing, Guangda went out to meet the royal army at the border and furnished it with supplies.

sentences.zh: 僧辯謂沈炯曰：「魯晉州亦是王師東道主人。」

translations.literal: Sengbian said to Shen Jiong: "Governor Lu of Jin is also a host for the royal army on the eastern route."
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian said to Shen Jiong: "Governor Lu of Jin is another host to the royal army on the eastern march."

sentences.zh: 仍率眾隨僧辯。

translations.literal: He then led his forces to follow Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops after Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 景平，加員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was given the additional post of Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat he was given the additional title of supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太建初，與儀同章昭達入峽口，招定安蜀等諸州鎮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian, he entered the gorge mouth with Commissioner Zhang Zhaoda and brought over the garrisons of Ding'an, Shu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taijian era under Chen Xuan, he entered the gorge with the commissioner Zhang Zhaoda and won over the garrisons of Ding'an, Shu, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時周圖江左，大造舟艦於蜀，並運糧青泥，廣達與錢道戢等將兵掩襲，縱火焚之，仍還本鎮。

translations.literal: At the time Northern Zhou was plotting against the lands south of the Yangzi, building ships in great numbers in Shu and also transporting grain through Qingni; Guangda with Qian Daoji and others led troops in a surprise raid, set fire and burned them, then returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou was then scheming against the south, building a great fleet in Shu and shipping grain through Qingni. Guangda, with Qian Daoji and others, led a surprise attack, burned the ships, and withdrew to his post.

sentences.zh: 廣達為政簡要，推誠任下，吏人便之。

translations.literal: Guangda's governance was simple and concise; he extended sincerity and trusted subordinates, and officials and commoners found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Guangda governed with simplicity and directness, treating subordinates with open trust, to the ease of officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 及秩滿，皆詣闕表請，於是詔申二年。

translations.literal: When his term expired, all came to court with memorials requesting [his retention], and therefore an edict extended it two years.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, petitioners thronged the court asking that he stay on, and an edict granted him two more years.

sentences.zh: 五年眾軍北伐，略淮南舊地，廣達與齊軍會於大峴，大破之，斬其敷城王張元範。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the combined armies marched north, reclaiming old Huainan territory; Guangda met Qi forces at Mount Daxian, routed them utterly, and beheaded their Prince of Fucheng Zhang Yuanfan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian the armies marched north to recover old Huainan. Guangda met Northern Qi forces at Mount Daxian, broke them completely, and beheaded Zhang Yuanfan, prince of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 進克北徐州。

translations.literal: He advanced and captured North Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed forward and took North Xu.

sentences.zh: 仍授北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Governor of North Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made governor of North Xu.

sentences.zh: 十年，授都督、合州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Area Commander and Governor of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed area commander and governor of He.

sentences.zh: 十一年，周將梁士彥圍壽春，詔遣中領軍樊毅、左衛將軍任忠等分部趣陽平、秦郡，廣達率眾入淮為掎角以擊之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Zhou general Liang Shiyan besieged Shouchun; an edict dispatched Central Palace Guard Commander Fan Yi, Left Guard General Ren Zhong, and others in separate columns toward Yangping and Qin commandery, while Guangda led forces into the Huai as a pincer to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Zhou general Liang Shiyan besieged Shouchun. The court sent the central palace guard commander Fan Yi, the left guard general Ren Zhong, and others in separate columns toward Yangping and Qin, while Guangda led troops into the Huai to strike in pincer.

sentences.zh: 周軍攻陷豫、霍二州，南北兗、晉等各自拔，諸將並無功，盡失淮南之地，廣達因免官，以侯還第。

translations.literal: Zhou armies captured Yu and Huo prefectures; North and South Yan, Jin, and the rest each withdrew; the generals all achieved nothing and wholly lost Huainan; Guangda was therefore dismissed from office and returned to his estate with his marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou forces overran Yu and Huo; the garrisons at North and South Yan, Jin, and elsewhere pulled out one after another. Every commander failed, and Huainan was lost entirely. Guangda was stripped of office and sent home, retaining only his noble title.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與南豫州刺史樊毅北討，克郭默城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he joined South Yuzhou Governor Fan Yi on the northern campaign and captured Guo Mo's fortress.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he joined the South Yu governor Fan Yi on a northern expedition and took the fortress of Guo Mo.

sentences.zh: 尋授平西將軍、都督郢州以上七州諸軍事，頓兵江夏。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Area Commander of the seven prefectures from Yingzhou upward, encamping his army at Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made general who pacifies the west and area commander over seven prefectures from Ying upward, with his army stationed at Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 周安州總管元景山征江外，廣達命偏師擊走之。

translations.literal: When Zhou's Area Supervisor of Anzhou Yuan Jingshan campaigned beyond the Yangzi, Guangda dispatched a detached column and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou area supervisor of An, Yuan Jingshan, campaigned beyond the Yangzi, Guangda sent a detached force and repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，為侍中，改封綏越郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he became Palace Attendant and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Suiyue commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide of Chen Houzhu he became palace attendant and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Suiyue.

sentences.zh: 尋為中領軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Central Palace Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed central palace guard commander.

sentences.zh: 及賀若弼進軍鍾山，廣達于白土岡置陣，與弼旗鼓相對。

translations.literal: When He Ruo led his army to Zhongshan, Guangda set his battle line at Mount Baitu, banners and drums facing He Ruo's.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruo advanced on Zhongshan, Guangda drew up his line at Mount Baitu, banners and drums arrayed squarely against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 廣達躬擐甲胄，手執桴鼓，率勵敢死而進，隋軍退走。

translations.literal: Guangda personally donned armor, hand holding the drumstick and drum, leading and encouraging the death-defying forward advance, and the Sui army retreated in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Guangda buckled on armor himself, drumstick in hand, rousing his men to die where they stood and drive forward. The Sui line broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 如是者數四。

translations.literal: This happened four times.
translations.idiomatic: Four times it happened thus.

sentences.zh: 及弼乘勝至宮城，燒北掖門，廣達猶督餘兵苦戰不息。

translations.literal: When He Ruo pressed his victory to the palace city and burned the North Side Gate, Guangda still directed the remaining troops in bitter fighting without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruo pressed his advantage to the palace walls and set fire to the North Side Gate, Guangda still rallied the remnant force and fought on without rest.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，乃解甲，面台再拜慟哭。

translations.literal: When dusk fell, he removed his armor, faced the palace terrace, bowed twice, and wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he laid down his armor, turned toward the palace terrace, bowed twice, and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 謂眾曰：「我身不能救國，負罪深矣。」

translations.literal: He said to the troops: "My person could not save the state; my guilt is deep indeed."
translations.idiomatic: He told his men: "I could not save the realm. My debt is beyond measure."

sentences.zh: 士卒皆涕泣歔欷，於是就執。

translations.literal: The soldiers all wept and sobbed, and thereupon he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers wept and sobbed together, and then he was taken.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，依例入隋。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, in accordance with precedent he entered Sui service.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenming of Chen Houzhu he entered Sui service according to the usual practice.

sentences.zh: 廣達追愴本朝淪覆，遘疾不療，尋以憤慨卒。

translations.literal: Guangda, brooding on his dynasty's ruin, fell ill and sought no cure; soon he died of indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: Brooding over the fall of his dynasty, Guangda fell ill and refused treatment. Before long he died of bitter grief.

sentences.zh: 尚書令江總撫柩慟哭，乃命筆題其棺頭，為詩曰：「黃泉雖抱恨，白日自留名，悲君感義死，不作負恩生。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Jiang Zong stroked the coffin and wailed in grief; he then ordered brush and ink to inscribe the head of the coffin, composing a poem that reads: "Though the Yellow Springs hold resentment, in the bright day one's name remains; grieving for you who died for righteous fidelity, not choosing to live ungrateful.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Jiang Zong caressed the coffin and wept aloud. He then had brush and ink brought to inscribe the head of the bier with a poem: "Though the underworld holds its grudges, fame endures in the light of day; I mourn you, who chose a loyal death rather than live on in ingratitude.

sentences.zh: 又制廣達墓銘，述其忠概。

translations.literal: He also composed an epitaph for Guangda, narrating his loyalty and dauntless spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote an epitaph for Lu Guangda, setting forth his steadfast loyalty and bold integrity.

sentences.zh: 初，隋將韓擒濟江，廣達長子世真在新蔡，乃與其弟世雄及所部奔擒，擒遣使致書招廣達。

translations.literal: At first, when Sui general Han Qin crossed the river, Guangda's eldest son Shizhen was at Xincai; he then with his younger brother Shixiong and their command went over to Qin, and Qin sent a messenger with a letter to recruit Guangda.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when the Sui general Han Qin crossed the Yangzi, Lu Guangda's eldest son Shizhen was at Xincai. Shizhen went over to Han Qin with his younger brother Shixiong and their troops, and Han Qin sent envoys with a letter summoning Lu Guangda.

sentences.zh: 廣達時屯兵都下，乃自劾廷尉請罪，後主謂曰：「世真雖異路中大夫，公國之重臣，吾所恃賴，豈得自同嫌疑之間乎？」

translations.literal: Guangda was then encamped at the capital; he therefore impeached himself before the Court of Review and asked punishment. Houzhu said: "Though Shizhen is an irregular associate grand master of the palace, you are a weighty minister of the state whom I rely upon — how can you put yourself among the suspected?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangda was then stationed at the capital. He impeached himself before the Court of Review and asked to be punished. Chen Houzhu said, "Though Shizhen has gone over to the enemy and holds the rank of irregular associate grand master of the palace, you are a pillar of the state whom I rely on — how can you treat yourself as though under suspicion?

sentences.zh: 加賜黃金，即日還營。

translations.literal: He was further granted gold and returned to camp the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu added a gift of gold, and Lu Guangda returned to his camp that same day.

sentences.zh: 廣達有隊主楊孝辯，時從廣達在軍中，力戰陷陣，其子亦隨孝辯揮刀殺隋兵十餘人，力窮，父子俱死。

translations.literal: Guangda had a squad leader Yang Xiaobian, who then followed Guangda in the army, fighting hard and breaking formations; his son also followed Xiaobian, wielding a blade and killing more than ten Sui soldiers; strength exhausted, father and son both died.
translations.idiomatic: Among Lu Guangda's men was a squad leader named Yang Xiaobian, then serving under him in the field. Yang fought his way deep into the enemy lines; his son fought beside him, cutting down more than ten Sui soldiers before their strength gave out. Father and son died together.

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶字元胤，蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe, courtesy name Yuanyin, was a man of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe, styled Yuanyin, came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 父諒，梁始興郡丞。

translations.literal: His father Liang was assistant magistrate of Shixing commandery under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao Liang served as assistant magistrate of Shixing under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 摩訶隨父之郡，年數歲而父卒，其姊夫蔡路養時在南康，乃收養之。

translations.literal: Mohe followed his father to the commandery; at a few years of age his father died; his sister's husband Cai Luyang was then at Nankang, and took him in to raise.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe went with his father to his post while still a small boy; when his father died, his brother-in-law Cai Luyang, then at Nankang, took him in and raised him.

sentences.zh: 稍長，果毅有勇力。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, he was resolute and possessed courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he proved resolute, brave, and strong.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，陳武帝赴援建鄴，路養起兵拒武帝，摩訶時年十三，單騎出戰，軍中莫有當者。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Chen Wudi went to aid Jianye; Luyang raised troops to resist the Emperor; Mohe was then thirteen years old, rode out alone to battle, and in the army none could stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Chen Wudi marched to relieve Jianye. Cai Luyang raised forces to oppose him; Mohe was only thirteen, yet rode out alone to fight, and none in the army could match him.

sentences.zh: 及路養敗，摩訶歸侯安都，常從征討，安都遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: When Luyang was defeated, Mohe joined Hou Andu, regularly followed on campaigns, and Andu treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai Luyang's defeat, Mohe entered Hou Andu's service and often rode with him on campaign; Hou Andu treated him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 及任約、徐嗣徽引齊兵為寇，武帝遣安都北拒齊軍于鍾山龍尾及北郊壇。

translations.literal: When Ren Yue and Xu Sihui led Qi troops as invaders, the Emperor sent Andu north to resist the Qi army at Zhongshan's Longwei and the North Suburban Altar.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Yue and Xu Sihui brought Northern Qi forces south to raid, Chen Wudi sent Hou Andu north to hold the Qi army at Longwei on Zhongshan and at the North Suburban Altar.

sentences.zh: 安都謂摩訶曰：「卿驍勇有名，千聞不如一見。」

translations.literal: Andu said to Mohe: "You have a reputation for fierce courage — a thousand hearers are not equal to one sight.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu said to Mohe, "Your name for fierce courage has gone ahead of you — hearing of it a thousand times is nothing beside seeing you once.

sentences.zh: 摩訶對曰：「今日令公見之。」

translations.literal: Mohe replied: "Today let the lord see it."
translations.idiomatic: Mohe answered, "Today Your Lordship shall see."

sentences.zh: 及戰，安都墜馬被圍，摩訶獨騎大呼，直沖齊軍，齊軍稍解去，安都乃免。

translations.literal: When battle came, Andu fell from his horse and was surrounded; Mohe alone on horseback shouted loudly, charged straight into the Qi army; the Qi army gradually dispersed, and Andu was spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting Hou Andu was thrown from his horse and surrounded. Mohe spurred forward alone, shouting, and drove straight into the Qi line until the enemy drew back and Andu was freed.

sentences.zh: 以平留異、歐陽紇功，累遷巴山太守。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Liu Yi and Ouyang He, he was repeatedly promoted to governor of Bashan.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in suppressing Liu Yi and Ouyang He, he rose in due course to governor of Bashan.

sentences.zh: 太建五年，眾軍北伐，摩訶隨都督吳明徹濟江攻秦郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, when the massed armies marched north, Mohe followed Area Commander Wu Mingche in crossing the river to attack Qin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taijian (573), during the great northern campaign, Mohe crossed the Yangzi with Area Commander Wu Mingche to strike at Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 時齊遣大將尉破胡等率眾十萬來援，其前隊有「蒼頭」、「犀角「、「大力」之號，皆身長八尺，膂力絕倫，其鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: At that time Qi sent the great general Wei Pohu and others leading a hundred thousand men to relieve them; their vanguard bore the names "Dark Head," "Rhino Horn," and "Great Strength" — all eight feet tall, with peerless brawn, and their spearhead very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi sent the great general Wei Pohu at the head of a hundred thousand men. Their vanguard units were called "Dark Head," "Rhino Horn," and "Great Strength" — giants eight feet tall, of unmatched strength, and their point was very keen.

sentences.zh: 又有西域胡，妙於弓矢，弦無虛發，眾軍尤憚之。

translations.literal: There was also a Western Regions barbarian, skilled with bow and arrow, every shot on target, and the armies especially feared him.
translations.idiomatic: With them was a man from the Western Regions, a master archer who never wasted a shot; the Chen armies feared him above all.

sentences.zh: 及將戰，明徹謂摩訶曰：「若殪此胡，則彼軍奪氣，君有關、張之名，可斬顏良矣。」

translations.literal: When battle was about to be joined, Mingche said to Mohe: "If this Hu is killed, their army will lose its spirit; you bear the name of Guan and Zhang — you can slay Yan Liang."
translations.idiomatic: As the armies were about to clash, Wu Mingche told Mohe, "Kill this archer and their spirit will break. You have the repute of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei — this is your chance to take off a Yan Liang's head."

sentences.zh: 摩訶曰：「願得識其形狀。」

translations.literal: Mohe said: "I wish to know his appearance."
translations.idiomatic: Mohe said, "I must know what he looks like."

sentences.zh: 明徹乃召降人有識胡者，雲胡絳衣，樺皮裝弓，兩端骨弭。

translations.literal: Mingche then summoned a defector who knew the Hu, who said the Hu wore crimson clothes, a birch-bark bow case, and bone nocks at both ends.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche called up a defector who knew the man and learned that he wore crimson, carried his bow in birch bark, and used bone nocks at either end of the string.

sentences.zh: 明徹遣人覘伺，知胡在陣，仍自酌酒飲摩訶。

translations.literal: Mingche sent men to reconnoiter, learned the Hu was in formation, and himself poured wine for Mohe to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche sent scouts to locate the archer in the enemy line, then poured Mohe a cup of wine himself.

sentences.zh: 摩訶飲訖，馳馬沖齊軍，胡挺身出陣前十餘步，彀弓未發，摩訶遙擲銑鋧，正中其額，應手而僕。

translations.literal: When Mohe had finished drinking, he spurred his horse and charged the Qi army; the Hu stepped forward more than ten paces before the formation, drew his bow but had not released, when Mohe from afar threw a throwing blade that struck him square on the forehead; he fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe drained the cup, wheeled his horse, and charged the Qi line. The archer stepped out a dozen paces ahead of the formation and was drawing his bow when Mohe hurled a hatchet from afar; it struck him in the forehead and he dropped where he stood.

sentences.zh: 齊軍「大力」十餘人出戰，摩訶又斬之，於是齊師退走。

translations.literal: More than ten "Great Strength" men of the Qi army came out to fight; Mohe cut them down again, and then the Qi army withdrew in flight.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen of the Qi "Great Strength" fighters came forward; Mohe cut them down as well, and the Qi army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 以功封廉平縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Earl of Lianping county.
translations.idiomatic: For this exploit he was created Earl of Lianping.

sentences.zh: 尋進為侯，位太僕卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to marquis and appointed Minister of Imperial Studs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to marquis and made minister of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 又隨明徹進圍宿預，擊走齊將王康得，以功除晉熙太守。

translations.literal: He again followed Mingche in advancing to besiege Suyu, routed the Qi general Wang Kangde, and for merit was appointed governor of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He went on with Wu Mingche to besiege Suyu, drove off the Qi general Wang Kangde, and for his service was made governor of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 九年，明徹進軍呂梁，與齊大戰，摩訶率七騎先入，手奪齊軍大旗，齊眾大潰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Mingche advanced on Luliang and fought a great battle with Qi; Mohe led seven horsemen in first, with his own hand seized the Qi army's great banner, and the Qi masses were greatly routed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (577) Wu Mingche marched on Luliang and fought a great battle with Qi. Mohe led seven horsemen in the van, snatched the enemy's great standard with his own hand, and the Qi forces collapsed.

sentences.zh: 以功授譙州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed governor of Qiao province.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made governor of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 及周武帝滅齊，遣其將宇文忻爭呂梁。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wudi destroyed Qi, he sent his general Yuwen Xin to contest Luliang.
translations.idiomatic: After Northern Zhou Wudi extinguished Qi, he sent his general Yuwen Xin to wrest Luliang from Chen hands.

sentences.zh: 忻時有精騎數千，摩訶領十二騎，深入周軍，從橫奮擊，斬馘甚眾。

translations.literal: Xin then had several thousand picked cavalry; Mohe led twelve horsemen, penetrated deep into the Zhou army, fought to and fro with fierce attacks, and cut heads and ears in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin had several thousand elite horsemen. Mohe took twelve riders, plunged deep into the Zhou line, and fought back and forth with such fury that the dead and wounded piled up around him.

sentences.zh: 及周遣大將王軌來赴，結長圍連鎖于呂梁下流，斷大軍還路。

translations.literal: When Zhou sent the great general Wang Gui to come to the rescue, he formed a long encirclement with chained boats on the lower reaches at Luliang and cut off the great army's return route.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou dispatched the great general Wang Gui in relief, Wang laid a long blockade with chained boats on the lower river at Luliang and severed the Chen army's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 摩訶謂明徹曰：「聞軌始鎖下流，其兩頭築城，今尚未立，公若見遣擊之，彼必不敢相拒。

translations.literal: Mohe said to Mingche: "I hear Gui has only just begun to chain the lower reaches and build fortifications at both ends, which are not yet established; if you would send me to strike them, they surely would not dare resist.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe said to Wu Mingche, "I hear Wang Gui has only begun to chain the river downstream and erect forts at either end — they are not finished yet. Send me against them now and they will not dare stand.

sentences.zh: 彼城若立，則吾屬虜矣。」

translations.literal: If those forts are established, then we will be captives.
translations.idiomatic: Once those forts stand, we are prisoners.

sentences.zh: 明徹奮髯曰：「搴旗陷陣，將軍事也；

translations.literal: Mingche bristled his beard and said: "Seizing banners and breaking formations — that is a general's affair;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche tugged at his beard and said, "Taking banners and breaking lines — that is the general's business;

sentences.zh: 長算遠略，老夫事也。」

translations.literal: long calculation and far-reaching plans — that is this old man's business."
translations.idiomatic: long-range planning is an old man's work.

sentences.zh: 摩訶失色而退。

translations.literal: Mohe changed color and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe paled and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 一旬之中，水路遂斷，周兵益至。

translations.literal: Within ten days the water route was cut off, and Zhou troops increased in arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the river route was closed and Zhou reinforcements kept arriving.

sentences.zh: 摩訶又請曰：「今求戰不得，進退無路，若潛軍突圍，未足為恥。

translations.literal: Mohe again requested: "Now we cannot seek battle, advance and retreat have no route; if we secretly break out of encirclement, it is not enough to be shame.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe pleaded again, "We cannot bring them to battle; there is no way forward or back. A stealthy breakout would be no disgrace.

sentences.zh: 願公率步卒乘馬輿徐行，摩訶驅馳前後，必使公安達京邑。」

translations.literal: I wish that you would lead foot soldiers riding in horse-litters at an easy pace; Mohe would charge before and behind, and surely make the lord safely reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Let you take the infantry in litters at an easy pace while I ride before and behind; I swear I will see you safely to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明徹曰：「弟計乃良圖也。

translations.literal: Mingche said: "Brother's plan is indeed a good scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche said, "Your plan is a good one.

sentences.zh: 然老夫受脤專征，今被圍逼，慚置無地。

translations.literal: Yet this old man received the war-meat and sole command of the campaign; now besieged and pressed, shame has no place to stand.
translations.idiomatic: But I took the war feast and sole command of this campaign; now, hemmed in, I have nowhere to hide my shame.

sentences.zh: 且步軍既多，吾為總督，必須身居其後，相率兼行，弟馬軍宜須在前。」

translations.literal: Moreover the foot army is numerous; as area commander I must personally be at the rear, leading all together in combined march; brother's horse army ought to be in front."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the foot soldiers are many; as commander I must bring up the rear and keep the column together — your cavalry should go in front.

sentences.zh: 摩訶因夜發，選精騎八千，率先衝突，自後眾騎繼焉。

translations.literal: Mohe therefore set out by night, selected eight thousand picked cavalry, took the lead in charging, and from behind the mass of cavalry followed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Mohe moved out with eight thousand picked horsemen, broke through in the lead, and the rest of the cavalry followed hard after.

sentences.zh: 比旦，達淮南。

translations.literal: By dawn they reached Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn they had reached Huainan.

sentences.zh: 宣帝征還，授右衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan recalled the campaign, he was appointed General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuan recalled the army and appointed Mohe general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝崩，始興王叔陵于殿內手刃後主，遂奔東府城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, the Prince of Shixing Shuling with his own hand in the palace hall stabbed Houzhu, then fled to Dongfu city.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xuan died, the Prince of Shixing, Chen Shuling, stabbed the crown prince in the palace hall and fled to the Eastern Palace fortress.

sentences.zh: 摩訶入受敕，乃率馬步數百趣東府城，斬之。

translations.literal: Mohe entered, received the edict, then led several hundred horse and foot to hasten to Dongfu city and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe received his orders in the palace, then led several hundred horse and foot to the Eastern Palace fortress and killed Shuling.

sentences.zh: 以功授車騎大將軍，封綏建郡公。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and enfeoffed as Duke of Suijian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and created Duke of Suijian.

sentences.zh: 叔陵素所蓄聚金帛累巨萬，後主悉以賜之。

translations.literal: The gold and silk Shuling had long amassed amounted to tens of thousands; Houzhu entirely bestowed it upon him.
translations.idiomatic: The gold and silk Chen Shuling had hoarded ran to immense sums; Chen Houzhu gave it all to Mohe.

sentences.zh: 改授侍中、驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Palace Attendant, Grand General of Cavalry and Chariots, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as palace attendant, grand general of swift cavalry, and left grand master of splendid virtue.

sentences.zh: 舊制三公黃合聽事置鴟尾。

translations.literal: By old regulation the three excellencies' yellow-folding offices for audiences had owl-tail finials.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom the three excellencies' yellow-folding reception halls bore owl-tail roof ornaments.

sentences.zh: 後主特詔摩訶開黃合，門施行馬，聽事寢堂，並置鴟尾。

translations.literal: Houzhu specially issued an edict to Mohe to open the yellow folding, with dismounting posts at the gate, and owl-tail finials on both reception hall and sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu specially authorized Mohe to use the yellow-folding gate, dismounting rails at his doorway, and owl-tail ornaments on both his reception hall and private quarters — honors normally reserved for the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 仍以其女為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: He furthermore made his daughter crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: He also married Mohe's daughter to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 會隋總管賀若弼鎮廣陵，後主委摩訶禦之，授南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Sui area commander He Ruobi garrisoned Guangling, Houzhu entrusted Mohe to defend against him and appointed him governor of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui area commander He Ruobi was stationed at Guangling; Chen Houzhu put Mohe in charge of the defense and made him governor of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年元會，征摩訶還朝，弼乘虛濟江，襲京口。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, at the New Year's assembly, Mohe was summoned back to court; Bi took advantage of the vacancy to cross the river and strike Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year's court of the third year of Zhenming (587), Mohe was recalled to the capital. He Ruobi seized the opening, crossed the Yangzi, and struck at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 摩訶請率兵逆戰，後主不許。

translations.literal: Mohe requested to lead troops to meet in battle; Houzhu did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe asked to take the field against him; Chen Houzhu refused.

sentences.zh: 及弼進鍾山，摩訶又曰：「弼懸軍深入，壘塹未堅，出兵掩襲，必克。」

translations.literal: When Bi advanced on Zhongshan, Mohe again said: "Bi's army hangs deep in enemy country, fortifications not yet firm; send troops in a surprise strike and he will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruobi pushed on to Zhongshan, Mohe said again, "His army is deep in hostile country and his defenses are not set — a surprise attack will take him.

sentences.zh: 又不許。

translations.literal: Again he did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Again Chen Houzhu refused.

sentences.zh: 及將出戰，後主謂曰：「公可為我一決。」

translations.literal: When they were about to go out to battle, Houzhu said: "You can fight one decisive battle for me.
translations.idiomatic: As the army was about to march out, Chen Houzhu told him, "You must win this battle for me.

sentences.zh: 摩訶曰：「從來行陣，為國為身，今日之事，兼為妻子。」

translations.literal: Mohe said: "In all my campaigns before, I fought for country and for myself; today's affair is also for wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: Mohe answered, "In every battle until now I have fought for the state and for myself; today I fight for my wife and children as well."

sentences.zh: 後主多出金帛賦諸軍，以充賞賜。

translations.literal: Houzhu greatly dispensed gold and silk to the armies as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu handed out gold and silk to the armies to swell their rewards.

sentences.zh: 令中領軍魯廣達陳兵白土岡，居眾軍南，鎮東大將軍任忠次之，護軍將軍樊毅、都官尚書孔范又次之，摩訶軍最居北。

translations.literal: He ordered Central Army Director Lu Guangda to deploy troops at White Earth Mound, placed south of the massed armies; Grand General Who Pacifies the East Ren Zhong next; Protector of the Army Fan Yi and Minister of Punishments Kong Fan next again; Mohe's army was northernmost.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Central Army Director Lu Guangda on White Earth Mound at the southern wing; Grand General Who Pacifies the East Ren Zhong came next, then Protector of the Army Fan Yi and Minister of Punishments Kong Fan; Mohe's corps held the northern end.

sentences.zh: 眾軍南北亙二十里，首尾進退不相知。

translations.literal: The massed armies stretched twenty li north and south; front and rear in advance and retreat did not know one another.
translations.idiomatic: The line ran twenty li from north to south; front and rear could neither coordinate advance nor retreat.

sentences.zh: 弼初謂未戰，將輕騎登山，望見眾軍，因馳下置陣。

translations.literal: Bi at first thought there would be no battle; he led light cavalry up the mountain, saw the massed armies, then galloped down to set formation.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi at first expected no fight; he rode light cavalry up a hill, saw the Chen line, and galloped down to deploy.

sentences.zh: 後主通於摩訶之妻，故摩訶雖領勁兵八千，初無戰意，唯魯廣達、田端以其徒力戰。

translations.literal: Houzhu had illicit relations with Mohe's wife; therefore though Mohe commanded eight thousand crack troops, at first he had no will to fight — only Lu Guangda and Tian Duan with their followers fought hard.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu had taken Mohe's wife as a lover; though Mohe still commanded eight thousand elite troops, he had no heart for the fight at first — only Lu Guangda and Tian Duan and their men battled fiercely.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼及所部行軍七總管楊牙、韓洪、員明、黃昕、張默言、達奚隆、張辯等甲士凡八千人，各勒陣以待之。

translations.literal: He Ruobi and his subordinate marching seven area commanders Yang Ya, Han Hong, Yuan Ming, Huang Xin, Zhang Moyan, Daxi Long, Zhang Bian and others with armored soldiers totaling eight thousand men each drew up formation to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi and seven subordinate area commanders — Yang Ya, Han Hong, Yuan Ming, Huang Xin, Zhang Moyan, Daxi Long, and Zhang Bian — with eight thousand armored men in all drew up and waited.

sentences.zh: 弼躬當魯廣達，麾下戰死者二百七十三人，弼縱煙以自隱，窘而復振。

translations.literal: Bi personally faced Lu Guangda; under his command two hundred seventy-three died in battle; Bi sent up smoke to hide himself, was hard pressed yet rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi himself engaged Lu Guangda; two hundred seventy-three of his men fell before he hid the field in smoke, rallied from distress, and came on again.

sentences.zh: 陳兵得人頭，皆走獻後主，求賞金銀。

translations.literal: Chen soldiers who obtained enemy heads all ran to present them to Houzhu, seeking gold and silver reward.
translations.idiomatic: Chen soldiers who took enemy heads ran to show them to Chen Houzhu and claim gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 弼更趣孔范，範兵暫交便敗走。

translations.literal: Bi then pressed Kong Fan; Fan's troops barely exchanged blows before fleeing in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi then turned on Kong Fan; Fan's men broke almost as soon as they met the attack.

sentences.zh: 陳軍盡潰，死者五千人。

translations.literal: The Chen army was entirely routed; five thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen army collapsed; five thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 諸門衛皆走，黃昕馳燒北掖門而入。

translations.literal: All gate guards fled; Huang Xin galloped, burned the North Side Gate, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards fled; Huang Xin burned through the North Side Gate and rode in.

sentences.zh: 員明禽摩訶以送弼，弼以刀臨頸，詞色不撓，乃釋而禮之。

translations.literal: Yuan Ming captured Mohe and delivered him to Bi; Bi put a blade to his neck, yet his words and bearing did not waver; he then released and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming seized Mohe and brought him to He Ruobi. He Ruobi set a blade to his throat, but Mohe's words and bearing never faltered; he released him and treated him with honor.

sentences.zh: 及城平，弼置後主於德教殿，令兵衛守，摩訶請弼曰：「今為囚虜，命在斯須，願一見舊主，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: When the city was pacified, Bi placed Houzhu in the Hall of Virtuous Teaching and set soldiers to guard; Mohe requested of Bi: "Now as prisoners our lives hang in an instant; I wish once to see my former lord — to die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, He Ruobi kept Chen Houzhu in the Hall of Virtuous Teaching under guard. Mohe begged He Ruobi, "We are captives now and live from moment to moment. Let me see my former sovereign once — then I can die without regret.

sentences.zh: 弼哀而許之。

translations.literal: Bi pitied him and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, He Ruobi agreed.

sentences.zh: 入見後主，俯伏號泣，仍於舊廚取食進之，辭訣而出，守衛者皆不能仰視。

translations.literal: He entered to see Houzhu, prostrated himself and wailed; then from the old kitchen he took food and presented it, took leave and went out — the guards all could not look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to Chen Houzhu, prostrated himself, and wept aloud. From the old kitchen he brought food and fed him, then took his leave; the guards could not bear to look up at him.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聞摩訶抗答賀若弼，曰：「壯士也，此亦人之所難。」

translations.literal: Sui Wendi heard Mohe's bold replies to He Ruobi and said: "A stalwart man — this too is what men find hard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Wendi heard how boldly Mohe had answered He Ruobi, he said, "A true warrior — that is something few men can manage.

sentences.zh: 入隋，授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Entering Sui, he was appointed Honorary Grand Master of the State with the same honors as the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Sui service he was made honorary grand master of the state with the same honors as the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 尋從漢王諒詣并州，同諒作逆，伏誅，年七十三。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Prince Han of Han to Bingzhou; together with the Prince he rebelled, was executed by law, age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the Prince of Han to Bingzhou, joined his rebellion, and was executed at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 摩訶訥於言，恂恂長者。

translations.literal: Mohe was slow of speech, a respectful elder in manner.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe was slow-spoken and courteous as an elder.

sentences.zh: 至於臨戎對寇，志氣奮發，所向無前。

translations.literal: Yet when facing the foe in battle his spirit blazed and wherever he turned none stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet facing the enemy in battle his spirit blazed and none could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，隨侯安都在京口，性好獵，無日不畋遊。

translations.literal: Before he had reached twenty, while following Hou Andu at Jingkou, he loved hunting and went out every day without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age, while with Hou Andu at Jingkou, he loved the hunt and went out every day without fail.

sentences.zh: 及安都征伐，摩訶功居多。

translations.literal: When Andu went on campaigns, Mohe's achievements were the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Andu's campaigns Mohe accounted for the lion's share of the victories.

sentences.zh: 子世廉，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Shilian had his father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilian had his father's mettle.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，及摩訶凶終，服闕後，追慕彌切。

translations.literal: Extremely filial by nature, after Mohe's violent end and when mourning was finished, his longing grew ever keener.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, after Mohe's execution and the mourning period had ended, his grief only deepened.

sentences.zh: 其父時賓故，脫有所言及，世廉對之，哀慟不自勝，言者為之歔欷。

translations.literal: When his father's old guests happened to speak of him, Shilian answered them, grief-stricken beyond bearing, and those who spoke were moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's old friends happened to mention him, Shilian would answer in such grief that the speakers themselves were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 終身不執刀斧，時人嘉焉。

translations.literal: All his life he would not take up blade or axe; men of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He never again touched blade or hatchet; men of the time honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 摩訶有騎士陳智深者，勇力過人，以平叔陵功，為巴陵內史。

translations.literal: Mohe had a knight Chen Zhishen, whose courage and strength surpassed others; for merit in pacifying Shuling he was made interior minister of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Among Mohe's riders was Chen Zhishen, a man of surpassing courage and strength; for his part in suppressing Chen Shuling he was made interior minister of Baling.

sentences.zh: 摩訶之戮也，其子先已籍沒，智深收摩訶屍，手自殯斂，哀感行路，君子義之。

translations.literal: When Mohe was executed, his son had already been confiscated and registered; Zhishen recovered Mohe's corpse and with his own hands prepared the burial — his grief moved passersby, and men of honor approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Mohe was put to death his son had already been seized and his property confiscated. Zhishen recovered Mohe's body and buried him with his own hands; his grief moved all who passed, and men of honor praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 潁川陳禹，亦隨摩訶征討。

translations.literal: Chen Yu of Yingchuan also followed Mohe on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu of Yingchuan also rode with Mohe on campaign.

sentences.zh: 聰敏有識量，涉獵經史，解風角兵書，頗能屬文，便騎射，官至王府諮議。

translations.literal: Clever and perceptive with judgment, he ranged through the classics and histories, understood wind-omens and military books, could compose essays fairly well, was skilled at riding and archery, and reached the rank of advisory officer of a princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and discerning, he read widely in the classics and histories, understood wind-omens and military treatises, wrote passable prose, rode and shot well, and rose to advisory officer in a princely household.

sentences.zh: 任忠字奉誠，小名蠻奴，汝陰人也。

translations.literal: Ren Zhong, courtesy name Fengcheng, childhood name Mannu, was a man of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhong, styled Fengcheng and known in youth as Mannu, came from Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 少孤微，不為鄉黨所齒。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and of humble station, he was not regarded by his village and district.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he was held in little regard by his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 及長，譎詭多計略，膂力過人，尤善騎射，州裏少年皆附之。

translations.literal: When grown, he was crafty and full of stratagems, his brawn surpassing others, especially skilled at riding and shooting; the young men of the commandery all attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he was shrewd and full of schemes, stronger than most, and especially skilled at riding and archery; the young men of the district rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 梁鄱陽王蕭範為合州刺史，聞其名，引置左右。

translations.literal: Liang's Prince of Poyang Xiao Fan was governor of He province; hearing his name, he summoned and placed him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fan, Prince of Poyang and governor of He province under the Liang, heard of him and took him into his personal service.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，忠率鄉黨數百人，隨晉熙太守梅伯龍討景將王貴顯于壽春，每戰卻敵。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Zhong led several hundred men of his village and followed Jinxi governor Mei Bolong in attacking Hou Jing's general Wang Guixian at Shouyang; in every battle he repelled the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he led several hundred local men with Jinxi governor Mei Bolong against Hou Jing's general Wang Guixian at Shouyang and beat back the enemy in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 會土人胡通聚眾寇抄，範命忠與主帥梅思立並軍討平之。

translations.literal: When the local man Hu Tong gathered a crowd to raid and plunder, Fan ordered Zhong and chief commander Mei Sili to join forces and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When a local leader named Hu Tong raised a band to raid the countryside, Xiao Fan sent Zhong and chief commander Mei Sili to join forces and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 仍隨範世子嗣率眾入援，會京城陷，旋戍晉熙。

translations.literal: He again followed Fan's heir Si in leading troops to enter relief; when the capital fell they turned to garrison Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the prince's heir Xiao Si south to relieve the capital; when the city fell they withdrew to garrison Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，授蕩寇將軍。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, he was appointed General Who Sweeps Away Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat he was appointed general who sweeps away bandits.

sentences.zh: 王琳立蕭莊，署忠為巴陵太守。

translations.literal: Wang Lin set up Xiao Zhuang and appointed Zhong governor of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin set up Xiao Zhuang as ruler, he appointed Zhong governor of Baling.

sentences.zh: 琳敗，還朝，授明毅將軍、安湘太守，仍隨侯瑱進討巴、湘。

translations.literal: When Lin was defeated, Zhong returned to court and was appointed Bright and Resolute General and governor of Anxiang; he still followed Hou Tian in advancing to attack Ba and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin's defeat Zhong returned to court and was made bright and resolute general and governor of Anxiang, then marched with Hou Tian against Ba and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 累遷豫甯太守，衡陽內史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to governor of Yuning and interior minister of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to governor of Yuning and interior minister of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 華皎之舉兵也，忠預其謀。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao raised troops, Zhong took part in the plot beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Zhong had been party to the plot from the start.

sentences.zh: 及皎平，宣帝以忠先有密啟於朝廷，釋而不問。

translations.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Emperor Xuan because Zhong had earlier sent a secret report to the court released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao's defeat Chen Xuan, knowing Zhong had secretly informed the court beforehand, pardoned him without punishment.

sentences.zh: 太建初，隨章昭達討歐陽紇于廣州，以功授直合將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian, he followed Zhang Zhaoda in attacking Ouyang He at Guangzhou and for merit was appointed Direct-Palace General.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taijian he joined Zhang Zhaoda's campaign against Ouyang He at Guangzhou and for his service was made direct-palace general.

sentences.zh: 遷武毅將軍、廬陵內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Martial and Resolute General and interior minister of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to martial and resolute general and interior minister of Luling.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，入為右軍將軍。

translations.literal: When his term ended he entered court as General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to court as general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 五年，眾軍北伐，忠將兵出西道，擊走齊曆陽王高景安於大峴，逐北至東關，仍克其東西二城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the massed armies marched north, Zhong led troops on the western route, routed Qi Prince of Liyang Gao Jing'an at Great Xian, pursued north to Dong Pass, and still captured its eastern and western cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (573), during the northern campaign, Zhong took the western route, routed the Qi Prince of Liyang Gao Jing'an at Great Xian, pursued him to Dong Pass, and captured both the eastern and western cities there.

sentences.zh: 進軍蘄、譙，並拔之。

translations.literal: Advancing he attacked Qi and Qiao and captured both.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to take Qi and Qiao as well.

sentences.zh: 徑襲合肥，入其郛。

translations.literal: He struck straight at Hefei and entered its outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: He struck straight at Hefei and entered its outer defenses.

sentences.zh: 進克霍州。

translations.literal: Advancing he captured Huo province.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and took Huo province.

sentences.zh: 以功授員外散騎常侍，封安復縣侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfu county.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was made supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and created Marquis of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 呂梁之喪師也，忠全軍而還。
