translations.literal: When the army was lost at Luliang, Zhong returned with his whole force intact.
translations.idiomatic: When the disaster struck at Luliang, Zhong brought his entire command back intact.

sentences.zh: 尋授忠都督壽陽、新蔡、霍州緣淮眾軍，霍州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Zhong area commander over the armies along the Huai at Shouyang, Xincai, and Huo province, and governor of Huo province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made area commander of the Huai-line armies at Shouyang, Xincai, and Huo province, and governor of Huo.

sentences.zh: 入為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 遷平南將軍、南豫州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and governor of South Yu province, with added area command.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general who pacifies the south and governor of South Yu, with area command added.

sentences.zh: 率步騎趣曆陽。

translations.literal: He led foot and horse in haste to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched foot and horse in haste to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 周遣王延貴率眾為援，忠大破之，生禽延貴。

translations.literal: Zhou sent Wang Yangui leading troops in relief; Zhong routed them greatly and captured Yangui alive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent Wang Yangui with reinforcements; Zhong routed him completely and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，進號鎮南將軍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When Houzhu succeeded, his title was advanced to General Who Guards the South, and he was granted one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Houzhu succeeded, Zhong was promoted to general who guards the south and granted a set of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 入為領軍將軍，加侍中，改封梁信郡公。

translations.literal: He entered court as Army Director and was added Palace Attendant; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Liangxin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as army director with palace attendant added to his title, and his fief was changed to Duke of Liangxin.

sentences.zh: 出為吳興內史。

translations.literal: He went out as interior minister of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as interior minister of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 及隋兵濟江、忠自吳興入赴，屯軍朱雀門。

translations.literal: When Sui troops crossed the river, Zhong entered from Wuxing to respond, encamping his army at the Vermilion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui forces crossed the Yangzi, Zhong marched in from Wuxing and encamped at the Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 後主召蕭摩訶以下於內殿定議，忠曰：「兵法客貴速戰，主貴持重。

translations.literal: Houzhu summoned Xiao Mohe and the rest to the inner hall to decide policy; Zhong said: "In military law the guest values swift battle, the host values holding firm.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu summoned Xiao Mohe and the other commanders to the inner hall for counsel. Zhong said, "In warfare the invader wants a quick fight and the defender wants to hold steady.

sentences.zh: 今國家足食足兵，宜固守台城，緣淮立柵。

translations.literal: Now the state has ample food and troops; we should firmly hold Terrace City and build palisades along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Our stores and armies are sufficient; we should hold Terrace City and build palisades along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 北軍雖來，勿與交戰，分兵斷江路，無令彼信得通。

translations.literal: Though the northern army comes, do not join battle with them; divide troops to cut the river route so their messengers cannot get through.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern armies come, do not meet them in the field; detach forces to cut the river routes so their couriers cannot pass.

sentences.zh: 給臣精兵一萬，金翅三百艘，下江徑掩六合。

translations.literal: Give me ten thousand picked troops and three hundred Gold-Wing warships; I will descend the river straight to strike Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Give me ten thousand picked troops and three hundred Gold-Wing warships, and I will go downriver and strike Liuhe directly.

sentences.zh: 彼大軍必言其度江將士已被獲，自然挫氣。

translations.literal: Their great army will surely say its men who crossed the river have already been captured, and naturally lose its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Their main force will hear that the troops who crossed have already been taken, and their spirit will collapse of itself.

sentences.zh: 淮南土人，與臣舊相知悉，今聞臣往，必皆景從。

translations.literal: The people of Huainan know me well from old days; hearing I am coming, they will surely follow in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Huainan know me of old; when they hear I am coming they will rally to me in numbers.

sentences.zh: 臣復揚聲欲往徐州，斷彼歸路，則諸軍不擊而自去。

translations.literal: I will again proclaim that I mean to go to Xuzhou and cut their route of return — then the armies will withdraw without being struck.
translations.idiomatic: I will spread word that I mean to march on Xuzhou and cut their retreat, and their armies will withdraw without our having to strike them.

sentences.zh: 待春水長，上江周羅睺等眾軍，必沿流赴援，此良計矣。」

translations.literal: Wait until the spring waters rise, and the upriver armies of Zhou Luohou and the rest will surely come downstream in relief — this is the good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the spring floods, and Zhou Luohou's upriver forces and the rest will come down to our aid — that is the sound plan.

sentences.zh: 後主不能從。

translations.literal: Houzhu could not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu would not take his advice.

sentences.zh: 明日欻然曰：「腹煩殺人，喚蕭郎作一打。」

translations.literal: The next day he suddenly said: "My belly is killing me — call Xiao for a bout.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he suddenly said, "This bellyache is killing me — send for Xiao and let us have a bout.

sentences.zh: 忠叩頭苦請勿戰，後主從孔範言，乃戰，於是據白土岡陣。

translations.literal: Zhong kowtowed and earnestly begged that they not fight; Houzhu followed Kong Fan's words and went to battle, and therefore deployed formation at White Earth Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong kowtowed and begged him not to fight, but Chen Houzhu listened to Kong Fan and gave battle, deploying on White Earth Mound.

sentences.zh: 及軍敗，忠馳入台，見後主，言敗狀，曰：「官好住，無所用力。」

translations.literal: When the army was defeated, Zhong galloped into the terrace, saw Houzhu, reported the defeat, and said: "Your Majesty stay well — there is nothing more I can do.
translations.idiomatic: When the army broke, Zhong galloped into the palace, saw Chen Houzhu, reported the defeat, and said, "Your Majesty had best stay put — there is nothing left for me to do.

sentences.zh: 後主與之金兩縢曰：「為我南岸收募人，猶可一戰。」

translations.literal: Houzhu gave him two belts of gold saying: "For me go south of the river and raise men — we can still fight once more."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu gave him two belts of gold and said, "Go south of the river for me and raise troops — we may still fight once more."

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「陛下唯當具舟烜，就上流眾軍，臣以死奉衛。」

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Your Majesty need only ready the boats and go upriver to the massed armies; I will guard you unto death."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "Your Majesty need only ready the boats and join the upriver armies; I will guard you with my life."

sentences.zh: 後主信之，敕忠出部分。

translations.literal: Houzhu believed him and ordered Zhong to go out and deploy the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu believed him and ordered him out to muster the troops.

sentences.zh: 忠辭云：「臣處分訖，即奉迎。」

translations.literal: Zhong declined saying: "When I have finished disposition I will come to escort you.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong excused himself, saying, "Once I have finished deploying the men I will come to escort you.

sentences.zh: 後主令宮人裝束以待忠，久望不至。

translations.literal: Houzhu had palace women dress and wait for Zhong; they waited long and he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu had the palace women dress and wait for Zhong; they waited a long time and he never came.

sentences.zh: 時隋將韓擒自新林進軍，忠率數騎往石子岡降之。

translations.literal: At that time Sui general Han Qin advanced from Xinlin; Zhong led several horsemen to Stonezi Mound and surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Sui general Han Qin was advancing from Xinlin; Zhong took a few horsemen to Stonezi Mound and surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 仍引擒軍共入南掖門。

translations.literal: He then led Qin's army together into the South Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought Han Qin's troops in through the South Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 台城平，入長安，隋授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Terrace City was pacified he entered Chang'an; Sui appointed him Honorary Grand Master of the State with the same honors as the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Terrace City he went to Chang'an, where the Sui court made him honorary grand master of the state with the same honors as the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: He died, age seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝后以散騎常侍袁元友能直言于後主，嘉之，擢拜主爵侍郎，謂群臣曰：「平陳之初，我悔不殺任蠻奴。

translations.literal: Afterward Sui Wendi because Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Yuan Yuanyou could speak bluntly to Houzhu praised him, promoted him to Chief of the Office for Enfeoffment, and said to the ministers: "At the beginning of pacifying Chen, I regretted not killing Ren Mannu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Yuan Yuanyou had spoken bluntly to Chen Houzhu, Sui Wendi praised him, promoted him to chief of the office for enfeoffment, and told his ministers, "When we first conquered Chen I regretted not having killed Ren Mannu.

sentences.zh: 受人榮祿，兼當重寄，不能橫屍，雲'無所用力'，與弘演納肝，何其遠也。」

translations.literal: Receiving honor and salary from others and also bearing heavy trust, yet unable to die transversely and saying 'there is nothing I can do' — how far from Hong Yan offering his liver!
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed rank and stipend and bore heavy trust, yet could not fall in battle and instead said 'there is nothing I can do' — how far that is from Hong Yan offering up his liver!

sentences.zh: 子幼武，位儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Youwu held the rank of Honorary Grand Master of the State with the same honors as the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youwu rose to honorary grand master of the state with the same honors as the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 樊毅字智烈，南陽湖陽人也。

translations.literal: Fan Yi, courtesy name Zhilie, was a man of Huyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi, styled Zhilie, came from Huyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖方興，梁散騎常侍、司州刺史、魚復縣侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fangxing was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, governor of Si province, and Marquis of Yufu county under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fan Fangxing served the Liang as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, governor of Si province, and marquis of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 父文熾，梁散騎常侍、東益州刺史、新蔡縣侯。

translations.literal: His father Wenci was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, governor of East Yizhou, and Marquis of Xincai county under the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan Wenci served the Liang as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, governor of East Yizhou, and marquis of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 毅家本將門，少習武，善騎射。

translations.literal: Yi's family was originally of the general's gate; in youth he practiced martial arts and was skilled at riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: The Fan family came from a military line; Yi trained in arms from youth and was skilled at riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，率部曲隨叔父文皎援台城。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he led his personal following and followed his uncle Wenjiao to relieve Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he led his household troops with his uncle Fan Wenjiao to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 文皎于青溪戰歿，毅赴江陵，仍隸王僧辯討河東王蕭譽，以功除右中郎將。

translations.literal: Wenjiao died in battle at Qingxi; Yi went to Jiangling and still followed Wang Sengbian in attacking the Prince of Hedong Xiao Yu, and for merit was appointed Right Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjiao fell at Qingxi; Yi went on to Jiangling and served under Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Hedong Xiao Yu, winning appointment as right central commandant.

sentences.zh: 代兄俊為梁興太守，領三州遊軍，隨宜豐侯蕭循討陸納於湘州。

translations.literal: He replaced his elder brother Jun as governor of Liangxing, commanded the roaming armies of three provinces, and followed the Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun in attacking Lu Na at Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced his elder brother Jun as governor of Liangxing, commanded the mobile forces of three provinces, and followed the Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun against Lu Na in Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 軍次巴陵，營頓未立，納潛軍夜至薄營，大噪，軍中將士皆驚擾，毅獨與左右數十人當營門力戰，斬十餘級，擊鼓申令，眾乃定焉。

translations.literal: The army halted at Baling; camps were not yet established when Na sent troops secretly by night to press the camp, raising a great clamor; officers and soldiers were all alarmed and disturbed — only Yi with several dozen men at his side held the camp gate and fought hard, cutting more than ten heads, beating drums to restore order, and then the masses settled.
translations.idiomatic: The army stopped at Baling before its camps were set when Lu Na sent men by night against the lines with a great uproar. The troops panicked — only Yi with a few dozen men held the camp gate, cut down more than ten of the enemy, beat the drums to restore order, and steadied the army.

sentences.zh: 以功封夷道縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yidao county.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was created Earl of Yidao.

sentences.zh: 尋除天門太守，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Tianmen and advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Tianmen and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 及西魏圍江陵，毅率郡兵赴援。

translations.literal: When Western Wei besieged Jiangling, Yi led commandery troops to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei besieged Jiangling, Yi led his commandery troops to the relief.

sentences.zh: 會魏克江陵，為後梁所俘，久之遁歸。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling he was taken by Later Liang; after long captivity he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling he was captured by Later Liang; after long imprisonment he escaped and made his way back.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝受禪，毅與弟猛舉兵應王琳，琳敗奔齊，太尉侯瑱遣使招毅，毅率子弟部曲還朝。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi received the abdication, Yi and his younger brother Meng raised troops to answer Wang Lin; when Lin was defeated and fled to Qi, Grand Marshal Hou Tian sent envoys to recruit Yi, and Yi led sons, younger brothers, and personal following back to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi took the throne, Yi and his younger brother Meng raised forces for Wang Lin; after Lin's defeat and flight to Qi, Grand Marshal Hou Tian sent to recruit Yi, and Yi returned to court with his sons, brothers, and household troops.

sentences.zh: 太建初，為豐州刺史，封高昌縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he was governor of Feng province and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaochang county.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taijian he was governor of Feng province and created marquis of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 入為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，眾軍北伐，毅攻廣陵楚子城，拔之，擊走齊軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the massed armies marched north, Yi attacked Chuzi city at Guangling and captured it, routing the Qi army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (573), during the northern campaign, Yi took Chuzi city at Guangling and drove off the Qi army.

sentences.zh: 及呂梁喪師，詔以毅為大都督，率眾度淮，對清口築城，與周人相抗。

translations.literal: When the army was lost at Luliang, an edict made Yi Grand Area Commander, leading troops across the Huai to build a city facing Qingkou and resist the Zhou men.
translations.idiomatic: After the disaster at Luliang he was made grand area commander, crossed the Huai with his troops, built a fort opposite Qingkou, and held the Zhou forces at bay.

sentences.zh: 霖雨城壞，毅全軍自拔。

translations.literal: Incessant rain ruined the walls; Yi withdrew the whole army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains collapsed the walls; Yi pulled the entire army out intact.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中領軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Central Army Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to central army director.

sentences.zh: 十一年，周將梁士彥圍壽陽，詔以毅為都督北討諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when Zhou general Liang Shiyan besieged Shouyang, an edict made Yi area commander of the northern punitive armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (579), when the Zhou general Liang Shiyan besieged Shouyang, he was made area commander of the northern punitive armies.

sentences.zh: 十三年，為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was governor of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (581) he became governor of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，改封逍遙郡公。

translations.literal: When Houzhu acceded, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Xiaoyao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Houzhu succeeded, his fief was changed to Duke of Xiaoyao.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant and Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as palace attendant and protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 及隋軍濟江，毅謂僕射袁憲曰：「京口、採石，俱是要所，各須銳卒數千，金翅二百，都下江中，上下防捍。

translations.literal: When Sui troops crossed the river, Yi said to Vice Director Yuan Xian: "Jingkou and Caishi are both vital points; each needs several thousand crack troops and two hundred Gold-Wing ships to descend the river from the capital and defend up and down the stream.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui forces crossed the Yangzi, Yi told Vice Director Yuan Xian, "Jingkou and Caishi are both critical — each needs several thousand elite troops and two hundred Gold-Wing ships sent down from the capital to guard the river above and below.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，大事去矣。」

translations.literal: If not so, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸從其議。

translations.literal: The generals all followed this plan.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders all agreed.

sentences.zh: 會施文慶等寢隋兵消息，毅計不行。

translations.literal: But Shi Wenqing and the rest suppressed news of the Sui troops, and Yi's plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But Shi Wenqing and his faction suppressed word of the Sui advance, and Yi's plan was never executed.

sentences.zh: 台城平，隨例入關，卒。

translations.literal: When Terrace City was pacified he entered the pass according to precedent and died.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the capital he went to the north as other captives did and died there.

sentences.zh: 毅弟猛字智武，幼俶儻，有幹略。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Meng, courtesy name Zhiwu, in youth was free-spirited and had capacity for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Fan Meng, styled Zhiwu, was bold and capable even as a boy.

sentences.zh: 及長，便弓馬，膽氣過人。

translations.literal: When grown, he was skilled with bow and horse and his daring surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he excelled at bow and horse and his courage outmatched others.

sentences.zh: 青溪之戰，猛自旦訖暮，與侯景軍短兵接戰，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: At the battle of Qingxi, Meng from dawn till dusk fought at close quarters with Hou Jing's army, killing and wounding very many.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingxi he fought hand to hand with Hou Jing's army from dawn till dusk, killing and wounding a great many.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，隨兄毅西上。

translations.literal: When Terrace City fell he followed his elder brother Yi west.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he went west with his brother Yi.

sentences.zh: 梁南安侯方矩為湘州刺史，以猛為司馬。

translations.literal: Liang's Marquis of Nan'an Fangju was governor of Xiang province and appointed Meng his chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fangju, Marquis of Nan'an and governor of Xiang province under the Liang, made Meng his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 會武陵王紀舉兵自漢江東下，方矩遣猛隨都督陸法和進軍拒之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling Ji raised troops from the Han river eastward, Fangju sent Meng to follow Area Commander Lu Fahe in advancing to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji marched east from the Han, Fangju sent Meng with Area Commander Lu Fahe to meet him.

sentences.zh: 猛手禽紀父子三人，斬於鰨中，盡收其船艦器械。

translations.literal: Meng with his own hand captured Ji and his father and son — three men — and beheaded them at Tazhong; he collected all their ships and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Meng personally seized Xiao Ji and his father and son — three men in all — and beheaded them at Tazhong, taking all their ships and gear.

sentences.zh: 以功封安山縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Earl of Anshan county.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was created Earl of Anshan.

sentences.zh: 進軍撫定梁、益。

translations.literal: Advancing he pacified Liang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and pacified Liang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 還遷司州刺史，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: On return he was transferred to governor of Si province and advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made governor of Si province and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 論曰：梁氏雲季，運屬雲雷，陳武帝杖旗掃難，經綸伊始，胡穎、徐度、杜棱、周鐵武、程靈洗等，或感會風雲，畢力驅馳之日，或擢自降附，乃贊興王之始，咸得配享清廟，豈徒然哉。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: In the declining season of the Liang, fortune belonged to cloud and thunder; Chen Wudi raised his banner to sweep away calamity — at the very beginning of ordering the realm, Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, Zhou Tiewu, Cheng Lingxi, and the rest either met the moment of wind and cloud and gave their full strength in the days of driving forward, or were promoted from among those who surrendered and thus aided the founding king from the start — all deserved to share in the clear temple; was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: In the Liang's last days, when fortune lay with storm and thunder, Chen Wudi raised his standard to clear away disaster. At the very founding of the realm, Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, Zhou Tiewu, Cheng Lingxi, and the rest — some seized the hour of upheaval and gave their all in the rush of conquest, others rose from among the surrendered and helped build the new dynasty from the start — all earned a place in the imperial temple. That was no empty honor.

sentences.zh: 沈恪行己之方，不踐非義之跡，子隆持身之節，無失事人之道，仁矣乎！

translations.literal: Shen Ke's way of conducting himself did not tread paths of injustice; Lu Zilong's integrity in holding himself never failed in the way of serving others — how humane!
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ke would not walk paths of injustice; Lu Zilong never failed in the duty owed to those he served — true humanity!

sentences.zh: 錢道戢、駱文牙、孫瑒、徐世譜、周敷、荀朗、周炅、魯悉達、廣達、蕭摩訶、任忠、樊毅等，所以獲用當年，其道雖異，至於功名自立，亦各因時。

translations.literal: Qian Daoji, Luo Wenya, Sun Yang, Xu Shipu, Zhou Fu, Xun Lang, Zhou Jiong, Lu Xida, Guangda, Xiao Mohe, Ren Zhong, Fan Yi and the rest — the reason they were employed in their day is that though their paths differed, each established merit in his own time.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daoji, Luo Wenya, Sun Yang, Xu Shipu, Zhou Fu, Xun Lang, Zhou Jiong, Lu Xida, Lu Guangda, Xiao Mohe, Ren Zhong, Fan Yi, and the rest won employment in their day because, though their roads differed, each made a name according to the times.

sentences.zh: 當金陵覆沒，抑惟天數，然任忠與亡之義，無乃致虧，與夫蕭、魯所行，固不同日。

translations.literal: When Jinling was overthrown, it was perhaps heaven's number; yet Ren Zhong's righteousness toward the perishing state was perhaps deficient — compared with what Xiao and Lu did, they are clearly not of the same day.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinling fell it was perhaps heaven's decree; yet Ren Zhong's loyalty to a dying state fell short — compared with what Xiao Mohe and Lu Guangda did, he stands on another day entirely.

sentences.zh: 持此百心，而事二主，欲求取信，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: Holding this hundredfold heart yet serving two lords — to seek trust, is it not hard?
translations.idiomatic: To keep one hundred loyalties in the heart yet serve two masters — how could trust be won?

sentences.zh: 首領獲全，亦為幸也。

translations.literal: That the leaders kept their lives whole was also fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That these commanders kept their lives at all was luck enough.
